# Map mode

Map mode explores a project through bounded outlines, symbol searches and source
reads. It builds the index automatically; there is no user `index` command.
The current CLI uses the shared dctx facade. Older storage and Git-based designs
in SPEC-MAP-MODE are not the current CLI contract.
dctx and this guide are Apache-2.0 (decision 078).

## Commands

```text
dctx map <map|find|neighbors|explain|read> [TARGET] [OPTIONS]
```

| Verb | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `map [TARGET]` | Outline the project root, a path or a node. |
| `find TARGET` | Search for a name or concept; quote multiword targets. |
| `neighbors TARGET` | Inspect a node's relations. |
| `explain TARGET` | Inspect one node's details. |
| `read TARGET` | Read a node's source. |

Copy node IDs from results: `m:sample.py` names a module and
`s:sample.py#PythonBeacon` names a symbol.

The following option descriptions follow `dctx map --help`
([source](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/crates/dctx-cli/src/map/args.rs)):

| Option | Meaning / bounds |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Facade JSON v2, including the precision label. |
| `--place PATH` | Place or worktree root; default: current directory. |
| `--budget TOKENS` | Output tokens, 1..2000; `explain` max: 1000. |
| `--depth N` | `map`: 1..3; `neighbors`: 1..2. |
| `--limit N --offset N` | `map`, `find`, `neighbors`: bound records; offset above 0 is refused. Pages use the next cursor. |
| `--kind fn,type,doc` | `find`: comma-separated node kinds. |
| `--in PATH` | `find`: restrict to a relative path. |
| `--edge calls,imports` | `neighbors`: comma-separated edge filter. |
| `--dir in\|out\|both` | `neighbors`: relation direction. |
| `--lines A-B --full` | `read`: help describes exact source lines; full permits 400. See limitation below. |
| `--rev SHA` | Refused: this map build does not link Git. |

The parser also accepts these `--kind` values: `method`, `struct`, `enum`,
`trait`, `impl`, `const`, `macro`, `class`, `interface`, `symbol`, `module`,
`package`, `place`, `test`. Edge names also include `contains`, `implements`,
`uses-type`, `tests`, `documents`, `reexports`.

The CLI currently translates `--lines A-B` into a line count (`B-A+1`) when
calling the facade; it does not forward the starting line. Exact arbitrary-range
selection is therefore **unverified**; do not rely on the help wording alone.
The token estimate is `ceil(2 * UTF-8 bytes / 7)`, not a tokenizer guarantee.

## Languages and precision

These extensions come from
[`Language::for_path`](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/crates/dctx-map-parse/src/domain/facts.rs).
That selector is case-insensitive; the current facade's separate extension
dispatch matches lowercase spellings, so use the spellings below for CLI input.

| Language | Extensions |
| --- | --- |
| Rust | `.rs` |
| JavaScript / JSX | `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.jsx` |
| TypeScript | `.ts`, `.mts`, `.cts` |
| TypeScript JSX | `.tsx` |
| Markdown | `.md`, `.markdown` |
| Python | `.py`, `.pyi` |
| Go | `.go` |
| Java | `.java` |
| C / C++ | `.c`, `.h`, `.cc`, `.cpp`, `.cxx`, `.hpp`, `.hh` |
| Configuration | `.json`, `.jsonc`, `.toml`, `.yaml`, `.yml` |
| C# | `.cs` |
| Kotlin | `.kt`, `.kts` |
| Ruby | `.rb`, `.rake`, `.gemspec` |
| PHP | `.php`, `.phtml`, `.inc` |
| Swift | `.swift` |

The default CLI extracts structural facts for all these languages. Rust uses a
line-oriented extractor; the others use the first-party structural lexers,
including the JS lexer for TypeScript/TSX and the Markdown heading extractor.
This is not a promise of exact semantic calls, type resolution or macro expansion.
An optional `syntax-rust` build links `syn` for supported Rust syntax, without
type checking; the feature alone does not change the CLI's default parser plan.

JSON answers expose `precision.coverage`, `precision.completion` and
`precision.parser` (the default parser identity is `dctx-structural/1`).
The [model](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/crates/dctx-map-model/src/domain/precision.rs) distinguishes
`structural`, `syntax` and `opaque` coverage from `complete`, `partial` and
`refused` completion. These labels describe extraction, separately from edge
confidence. Unsupported extensions provide no extracted symbols; the smoke test
checks empty records for `OpaqueBeacon` in `sample.unknown`.

## Index, cache and privacy

Each invocation opens a facade session, takes a strict snapshot and queries its
ephemeral index. Repeated processes share the host cache root, not a persistent
CLI graph database. Identity uses dctx's first-party SHA-256 and file metadata,
without Git object IDs. The retired per-worktree SQLite cache selector
(`map/storage.rs`) has been deleted: queries do not create `~/.cache/dctx/map`,
and the CLI does not read `DCTX_MAP_CACHE`.

The shared cache stores `ledger.v1` and `policy.v1`. Set `DCTX_CACHE_DIR` to an
absolute path to override its root. Otherwise it is:

| Platform | Cache root |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | `~/Library/Caches/dctx/v2` |
| Windows | `%LOCALAPPDATA%/dctx/Cache/v2` |
| Other | `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dctx/v2`, or `~/.cache/dctx/v2` |

The implemented lifecycle follows
[DX-ARCH-08](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/docs/design/ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md): time-based expiry, a system
size cap and an automatic cleaner. Defaults are 7 days for idle overlays/previews,
30 days for unpinned roots and 1 day for staging; the hard cap is 2 GiB, the soft
watermark 1.5 GiB and the eviction target 1.2 GiB. These are cache policies, not
a claim that every map query persists those object types.

```sh
dctx cache status --json
dctx cache gc --dry-run
dctx cache purge --root /absolute/project/path --dry-run
dctx cache purge --all --dry-run
dctx cache config auto off --max-bytes 1000000 --ttl-days 7
dctx cache auto
```

`status` accepts `--root PATH`; `gc` accepts `--root PATH`, `--max-bytes N` and
`--legacy`. Applying `purge` requires `--yes` and either `--root PATH` or `--all`.
`cache config` without arguments shows persisted policy; `auto on|off` controls
auto-clean, and `--max-bytes` can only tighten the cap. Pack, map, template,
plugin and TUI commands run one bounded cleanup when due (daily by default).
`--no-auto-clean` or `DCTX_AUTO_CLEAN=0` disables that slice.

Ignored files are excluded before content reads; omitted files may have metadata
listed but their content is never read. The core never reads `.git/` or runs Git
(decision 078). The intended `.gitignore` contract is rules only, not Git metadata.
**Unverified:** automatic `.gitignore` rule loading in this facade CLI path:
`host.rs` supplies `RuleTexts::default()`, with no local/global rule texts.
Do not assume project-specific ignore rules were loaded by this map command.
The optional Git plugin has separately disclosed authority; see [Plugins](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/plugins/).

## Two worked examples

These fixtures and output fragments are copied from
[`map_cli.rs`](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/crates/dctx-cli/tests/map_cli.rs). The test checks fragments,
not full transcripts; the output blocks below are excerpts, without invented
columns or counts. Create a project containing `sample.py`:

```python
def PythonBeacon():
    return 1
```

From that project, outline its module:

```sh
dctx map map m:sample.py --depth 2 --budget 2000
```

Expected output contains:

```text
s:sample.py#PythonBeacon
```

For the second example, add `sample.unknown` with:

```python
def OpaqueBeacon():
    return 1
```

Search the unsupported source extension:

```sh
dctx map find OpaqueBeacon --json
```

Expected JSON contains this exact fragment and does not contain `OpaqueBeacon`:

```text
"records":[]
```

For crate responsibilities and optional parser dependencies, see the
[crate map](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/crate-map/).

---
url: https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/agents/
title: Agent snippet
source: https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/docs/guides/AGENTS-SNIPPET.md
---

# AGENTS.md snippet: task context from dctx

Paste the section below into a project's `AGENTS.md` (or `CLAUDE.md`) so coding agents start from dctx context.
This repository keeps its own agent files out of git, so the snippet lives here.

## Notes for coding agents

Before editing, pull the code your task names, cut to a budget:

```sh
dctx pack --for "$TASK" --budget 3000
```

`$TASK` is the task or card text. dctx runs `map find` on the names the text mentions (backticked words, snake_case,
camelCase, `a::b`, then longer plain words), then `map neighbors` and `map read` on the best hits, and prints whole lines
until the budget is spent. The budget is in estimated tokens, ceil(2 × UTF-8 bytes / 7), not a tokenizer count. The last
line reports the estimate and how many lines were dropped. Exit 1 means no name in the text matched the index.

For a card file, `tools/cardgen/context.sh CARD [PLACE] [BUDGET]` prints the card followed by this context.
Then narrow with `dctx map find`, `dctx map neighbors <id>` and `dctx map read <id>` as needed (`dctx map --help`).

---
url: https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/plugins/
title: Plugins guide
source: https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/docs/guides/PLUGINS.md
---

# Plugins

A plugin adds commands or hooks through a bounded, versioned JSON protocol over
stdio. The host brokers its requested effects; installation, enablement,
capability consent and execution admission are separate steps. Bundled code can
run as a worker of the same executable; independently installed artifacts use
the plugin protocol. Availability is limited as described below.
dctx, the bundled Git plugin and this guide are Apache-2.0 (decision 078).

## Bundled Git plugin and consent

The default CLI includes `dctx/git` version `1.0.0`, with alias `dctx git` and
the verbs `status` and `protect`. The catalog defaults to enabled. A fresh CLI
without a consent record reports `enabled` with `needs-consent`; shipping the
worker does not grant its capabilities or guarantee that it can launch.
`dctx git` is a plugin alias, not a general Git passthrough.

The [bundled manifest capabilities](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/crates/dctx-cli/src/plugin/bundled.rs)
disclose these grants:

| Capability | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Required `file.read` | Project `.gitignore`, at most 1,048,576 bytes. |
| Required `file.write` | Existing project `.gitignore` only (`create=false`); growth at most 4,096 bytes, total at most 1,052,672 bytes. |
| Optional `program.run` | Program `git`, operation `git.add-ignore`, resource `git-admin:stage-ignore`, output at most 65,536 bytes. |
| Outputs / network | Neither requested. |

This narrow optional Git recipe belongs to the plugin boundary. The map/core
does not run Git, read `.git/` or use Git hashes for identity (decision 078).

Review the requested capabilities before approving:

```sh
dctx plugin list
dctx plugin info dctx/git --json
dctx plugin enable dctx/git --approve
dctx plugin disable dctx/git
```

`--approve` records consent for the displayed capability set. New installations
remain inactive until enabled; combined `install --enable` requires `--approve`.
Capability expansion can require fresh consent. Explicit disable persists
across updates. `enable --project PATH` scopes consent to a project; omitting it
uses user scope. `disable --project PATH` is accepted/reported, but the current
CLI disable operation is user-wide.

The desktop presents these states:

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `enabled` | Enabled in the registry; execution still requires admission. |
| `needs-consent` | Review and approve the requested capabilities. |
| `disabled` | Disabled by the user. |
| `failed` | A failure is reported; inspect the last failure message. |

The CLI additionally separates enablement (`inactive`, `enabled`, `disabled`)
from consent (`inactive`, `needs-consent`, `granted`, `disabled`) and reports
worker availability. A strict build lists the bundled catalog as disabled,
with consent `unavailable` and worker `excluded`.

## CLI reference

These are the command shapes from the plugin help renderer
([`render.rs`](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/crates/dctx-cli/src/plugin/render.rs)) and
[`parse.rs`](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/crates/dctx-cli/src/plugin/parse.rs):

```text
dctx plugin search [query] [--refresh] [--json]
dctx plugin install <owner/repo>[@version] [--enable --approve] [--json]
dctx plugin install --url <https-url> --id <publisher/name> [--json]
dctx plugin install --file <bundle> --id <publisher/name> [--json]
dctx plugin list [--json]
dctx plugin info <id> [--json]
dctx plugin enable <id> [--project <path>] [--approve] [--json]
dctx plugin disable <id> [--project <path>] [--json]
dctx plugin remove <id> [--json]
dctx plugin update [<id>] [--version <version>] [--check] [--json]
dctx plugin verify [<id>] [--refresh-trust] [--json]
dctx plugin run <id> -- <args>
dctx git <status|protect>
```

`dctx plugin`, `dctx plugin help`, `--help` and `-h` show plugin help.
Search accepts one query argument; quote phrases. Search and list use cached
metadata; `search --refresh` requests a fetch. List and help start no worker,
fetch nothing and do not create a project `.dctx/` directory.

Install accepts exactly one source: repository locator, HTTPS manifest URL or
offline bundle. URL/file sources require `--id`; the parser also accepts
`--enable --approve` with those sources. `update --check` reports a candidate
without downloading; omitting the ID in update/verify selects the bundled plugin.
`verify --refresh-trust` requests a revocation freshness check. Bundled updates
come with the containing CLI/app release. `remove` masks the bundled copy when
applicable. The current product's offline limits still apply to these commands.

`run` requires the `--` separator. The Git alias rejects that separator.
The parser recognizes `--json` for plugin and alias requests, including `run`,
and strips it before forwarding plugin arguments.

## Desktop: Settings > Plugins

Open **Settings > Plugins** to inspect bundled/installed source, version,
state, requested capabilities and the last failure. **Refresh plugins** reloads
the list. **Enable** and **Disable** call the host management API.
**Grant consent** opens a review dialog with plugin ID, version, artifact
SHA-256, capability descriptions and exact grants/bounds. **Confirm grant**
records user-wide consent for all projects; **Cancel** closes the dialog.
**Check for update** reports cached information and explicitly states that
online discovery is unavailable. These behaviors are implemented in
[`plugins.ts`](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/apps/dctx-desktop/src/plugins.ts); opening settings does
not itself execute plugin code or fetch from a network.

## Strict build

The [`dctx` library](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/crates/dctx/Cargo.toml) includes the optional
`plugin-runtime` feature in its defaults. Hosts requiring the engine without
that runtime must disable defaults and select `pack`, `map`, `templates`, `fs`,
`segments`, `cache` as needed. The runtime adds the host, platform and protocol
dependencies; sessions still require an explicit host.

For the [CLI](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/crates/dctx-cli/Cargo.toml), select
`--no-default-features --features strict` when building. Cargo features are
additive: selecting `strict` alone leaves defaults enabled. This composition
excludes `dctx-plugin-host`, `dctx-plugin-platform` and `dctx-plugin-git` from
normal dependencies. Management metadata/protocol/distribution code remains;
strict does not mean that every crate whose name contains `plugin` disappears.

## Trust and signatures

Distribution verifies detached Ed25519 signatures over domain-separated exact
manifest/index bytes, checks SHA-256 artifact integrity, and uses pinned
publisher keys, revocation freshness and rollback checks. A key downloaded
beside an artifact is not an independent trust anchor. Verification does not
grant capabilities or establish confinement. The production verifier never
signs or generates keys; signing belongs only in separate release tooling
(test fixtures use test keys). **Unverified:** a completed production release
signing tool in this checkout; the design describes it as separate work.
The product CLI currently supplies no index key and no TLS network adapter.

## What is not yet available

- Qualified native plugin launch on any OS. Linux has restricted-process
  building blocks, but arbitrary third-party ELF launch remains unsupported;
  macOS lacks the reviewed Seatbelt/initial-exec composition; Windows and other
  targets are unsupported. The platform provider also refuses bundled launch
  and the Git recipe. A consent record cannot bypass these admission failures.
- Online discovery, downloads and updates in the current product wiring.
  Search can inspect cached metadata and the distribution engine supports
  verified offline bundles, but network refresh needs a configured trust key
  and network adapter. The desktop explicitly reports offline update discovery.
- Public plugin publication through this CLI. There is no `plugin publish`
  command. The default discovery URL is `https://example.invalid/dctx/index.json`;
  a live public registry/release publication is **unverified**. Local index
  tooling and signed fixture tests do not establish public availability.

Sources: [plugin design](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/docs/design/PLUGINS.md),
[native platform limits](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/crates/dctx-plugin-platform/README.md),
[Ed25519 verification](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/crates/dctx-plugin-distribution/src/domain/signature.rs),
and the [crate map](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/crate-map/).

---
url: https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/exit-codes/
title: CLI exit codes
source: https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/docs/CLI-EXIT-CODES.md
---

# CLI exit codes

`dctx map`, `dctx pack`, `dctx mcp`, `dctx languages`, an unknown command and a non-UTF-8 argument follow one contract:

| Code | Meaning | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | ok: the command answered | a `find` page, including one with no hits; `--help` |
| 1 | no result: the command ran, but the named target or input has no answer | `map read m:nope.py` (an id not in the index); `map read logo.png` (a binary file); `pack` of a directory with no packable file |
| 2 | usage: the arguments are wrong | an unknown command or flag; a missing target; `--depth 9`; an empty `find` query; a stale `--cursor`; `m:../outside`; a non-UTF-8 argument |
| 3 | index error: the place, source, cache or index could not be opened, read, built or written | `--place /no/such/dir`; a corrupt or busy cache; a source over `DCTX_MAX_SOURCE_BYTES`; an `--output` file that cannot be written |

Every failure prints two lines on stderr: `❌ Error: <what went wrong>` (prefixed with the command, as `map: …`), then `hint: <what to do next>`. No input should reach a Rust panic; `crates/dctx-cli/tests/cli_errors.rs` and `<repo>/scripts/checks/V1-5.zsh` run twelve bad inputs and assert the code, the message, the hint and the absence of `panicked`.

## Details

- An id the index does not hold is a facade outcome (`gone`), not an error. `dctx map` prints the `gone` page on stdout, then exits 1 with the hint. `dctx mcp` returns the same page to the client as a normal tool result.
- An empty `find` or `grep` page is an answer and exits 0. Exit 1 is for a named target that is not there.
- A binary target is detected before the scan: a NUL byte in the first 8 KiB of the file named by `map`, `skeleton`, `explain` or `read` (path or `m:` id). `neighbors` and `path` still accept such a module, since source files can import it.
- `dctx pack` exits 1 only when no view filter is set (`--ext`, `--include`, `--exclude`, `--binary`, `--empty`, `--non-empty`, `--large`, `--small`, `--hidden`, `--debug-ignored`). A filter that matches nothing still prints an empty page and exits 0. The page and the `pack bytes=…` line are printed before the exit-1 message. `pack` exit 3 covers source, scan, render and output failures.
- A reader that closes stdout early (`dctx pack . | head -1`) ends the run with exit 0 and no message, as `cat` does; every other failure keeps its code.
- `dctx pack --for <TEXT>` exits 1 when no name in TEXT matched the index (the page is printed first), 2 for a bad flag or a `--budget` outside 100..100000 (or `--budget` without `--for`), and 3 when PATH is not a directory or the index fails.
- `dctx mcp PATH` exits 3 when PATH cannot be entered and 2 for any other argument. Once serving, a failed tool call goes back to the client as a result with `isError: true`; the server exits 0 at end of input.
- A facade refusal of the query (`InvalidRequest`, `BudgetTooSmall`, `StaleContinuation`, `Stale`, `UnsupportedCapability`, `UnsupportedVersion`) is 2; `PolicyDenied` and `PolicyUnavailable` are 1; every other facade error, and every error of the snapshot build, is 3. The mapping is `dctx_cli::exit::from_facade`.
- `map hubs`, `map path` and `map export` report their facade errors as text: an `unknown id` end of `map path` is 1, anything else 3.

## Outside the contract

These commands keep their earlier behaviour, exit 1 for every failure, with no hint line:

- `dctx cache …` and `dctx template …`;
- the legacy snapshot `dctx PATH` once its arguments parse (a bad snapshot flag is exit 2);
- `dctx plugin …` and `dctx git …`, which return the plugin host's own codes.

---
url: https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/privacy/
title: Privacy guarantees
source: https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/docs/ADR-014-Privacy-Guarantees-and-Ignore-Semantics.md
---

# ADR-014: Privacy Guarantees & Ignore Semantics

**Status:** ✅ IMPLEMENTED
**Date:** 2026-02-02
**Approved:** 2026-02-02
**Implemented:** 2026-02-02 (WO-050 through WO-054)
**Deciders:** Operator, AI Assistant
**Context:** Phase 10.6 - Safety-Critical Privacy & Performance Audit

---

## Context and Problem Statement

Users trust `dctx` with their entire codebases, including sensitive files like `.env`, `.git/`, API keys, credentials, and proprietary source code. Our ignore and omit systems were implemented primarily for output cleanliness and token efficiency, but we have not formally guaranteed that ignored files are **NEVER** read into memory.

**Critical Questions:**
1. Are ignored files (`.env`, credentials) ever read into memory?
2. Does the `--debug-ignored` flag compromise privacy?
3. What is the semantic difference between IGNORE and OMIT?
4. Can template variables accidentally trigger file reads on ignored files?
5. Do we recurse into ignored folders (performance impact)?

**Risk:** Without formal privacy guarantees, users cannot trust `dctx` with sensitive codebases. A single accidental file read could expose credentials, leak proprietary code, or violate security policies.

---

## Decision Drivers

* **Privacy First:** Ignored files must NEVER be read, regardless of flags or configuration
* **Performance:** Ignored folders must be skipped entirely (no recursion)
* **Semantic Clarity:** IGNORE vs OMIT must have clear, enforced meanings
* **Debug Transparency:** Users must be able to verify their ignore rules work correctly
* **Template Safety:** Custom templates must not accidentally trigger I/O on ignored files
* **Zero Trust:** Assume users handle classified/sensitive information

---

## Considered Options

### Option 1: Status Quo (No Formal Guarantees)
* **Pro:** No code changes required
* **Pro:** Current behavior is already safe (but undocumented)
* **Con:** No formal verification or tests
* **Con:** Users cannot trust the system
* **Con:** Template variables could be unsafe in the future
* **Verdict:** ❌ Rejected - Privacy must be provable, not assumed

### Option 2: Full Privacy Audit + Formal Guarantees (SELECTED)
* **Pro:** Provable privacy through code analysis and tests
* **Pro:** Clear semantic distinction between IGNORE and OMIT
* **Pro:** Template variable safety system prevents accidental reads
* **Pro:** Performance optimizations (skip ignored folders)
* **Pro:** Debug mode that doesn't compromise privacy
* **Con:** Requires implementation work (2-3 hours)
* **Verdict:** ✅ **SELECTED** - Only acceptable solution for sensitive codebases

### Option 3: Encryption-Based Approach
* **Pro:** Could encrypt ignored file contents in memory
* **Con:** Massive complexity, performance overhead
* **Con:** Doesn't solve the problem (still reading files)
* **Verdict:** ❌ Rejected - Overengineered, doesn't address root issue

---

## Decision Outcome

**Chosen Option:** Option 2 - Full Privacy Audit + Formal Guarantees

We will implement a three-tier rule system with formal privacy guarantees:

---

## Rule System Definition

| Rule Type | Directory Tree Visibility | File Content Section | Recurse into Folders? | Read File into Memory? |
|-----------|---------------------------|----------------------|----------------------|------------------------|
| **IGNORE** (default) | ❌ Hidden | ❌ Hidden | ❌ NO (skip entirely) | ❌ **NEVER** |
| **IGNORE** (`--debug-ignored`) | ✅ Shown with `[IGNORED]` marker | ❌ Hidden | ✅ YES (for diagnostics) | ❌ **NEVER** |
| **OMIT** (always) | ✅ Shown (normal) | ⚠️ `[Content omitted by pattern rules]` | ✅ YES | ❌ **NEVER** |

---

## Semantic Definitions

### IGNORE
**Meaning:** "This file/folder does not exist for our purposes."

**Use Cases:**
- `.git/` - Version control internals
- `node_modules/`, `target/`, `__pycache__/` - Build artifacts
- `.env`, `.secrets` - Credentials and sensitive configuration
- `*.log`, `*.tmp` - Temporary files

**Behavior:**
- Default: Not visible in tree, not in content, folder not recursed
- Debug Mode: Visible in tree with `[IGNORED]` marker, folder recursed, but files never read
- Configuration: `.dctxignore` (project) or `~/.config/dctx/ignore` (global)

### OMIT
**Meaning:** "This file exists and is relevant to the project structure, but we don't care about its contents."

**Use Cases:**
- `package-lock.json`, `Cargo.lock` - Lockfiles (structure matters, content doesn't)
- `*.svg` - Image files (relevant to project, but binary/verbose)
- `go.sum`, `yarn.lock` - Dependency checksums

**Behavior:**
- Always visible in directory tree (with metadata)
- Content section shows: `[Content omitted by pattern rules]`
- File is listed but never read into memory

### Debug Mode (`--debug-ignored`)
**Purpose:** Allow users to verify their ignore rules are working correctly.

**Behavior:**
- Temporarily treats IGNORE rules as OMIT rules for visibility
- Shows ignored files/folders in directory tree with `[IGNORED]` marker
- Recurses into ignored folders to show structure
- **CRITICAL:** Files are still NEVER read into memory
- Grayed-out metadata: SIZE from `stat()` only, never from content reading
- No LINES count (would require reading file)

### SENSITIVE (strict deny, v1)
**Meaning:** "This file holds credentials. No dctx command ever reads, hashes, indexes or prints its bytes."

**Shapes** (final path component, ASCII case-insensitive; the single list is
`dctx_core::filter::is_secret_shaped_name`):
- env files: `.env`, `.env.*`, `*.env`, `.envrc`
- keys, certificates and keystores: `*.pem`, `*.key`, `*.p12`, `*.pfx`, `*.jks`, `*.keystore`
- SSH private keys: `id_rsa`, `id_dsa`, `id_ecdsa`, `id_ed25519`, and those names with a `_`/`-` suffix
  without a dot (`id_rsa_deploy`); `id_rsa.pub` is not matched
- credentials: `credentials`, `credentials.<data>`, `*.credentials.json`, `secrets.<data>`
  (data = `json`, `yaml`, `yml`, `toml`, `ini`, `xml`); `credentials.py` and `secrets.rs` stay ordinary source
- token files: `.netrc`, `_netrc`, `.npmrc`, `.pypirc`, `.pgpass`, `.htpasswd`, `.git-credentials`

**Behavior:**
- The file stays listed by name (pack tree, map inventory) with its content omitted, and is never read.
- Applies whether or not the file is git-tracked, to every surface: `pack` (all view filters, including
  `--include`, `--ext`, `--hidden` and `--debug-ignored`), every `dctx map` verb (map, find, read, explain,
  skeleton, grep, neighbors, hubs, path, export; by stable id or by raw path; with or without `--in`) and the
  `dctx mcp` tools, which run the same code path.
- Enforced in the map policy (`PolicyView::decide`), again before any map read (`Session::read_verified`),
  in map grep, in the pack scan (`dctx-pack` snapshot) and in the `dctx-map-query` source adapter.
- **No override.** v1 has no `--allow-sensitive` flag, and repository or global rule files cannot
  re-include these shapes. dctx decides by name only; it does not scan contents, so a secret pasted into an
  ordinary source file is not detected.

**Verification:** `crates/dctx/tests/map_sensitive_files.rs`, the unit tests next to
`is_secret_shaped_name`, `PolicyView::decide` and the pack scan, and the end-to-end check
`<repo>/scripts/checks/V1-1.zsh` (a git-tracked fixture with one canary per shape, run against every command).

### `.git` (hard guard, v1)
Any path with a `.git` segment, at any depth, is excluded by `PolicyView::decide` before the rule layers are
consulted, so `!.git/`, `!.g*/` or `!nested/.git/**` in `.gitignore` or `.dctxignore` cannot re-include it: the
map verbs never list or read it, and `Session::read_verified` refuses it too. `pack` excludes it as well
(`dctx-pack` snapshot); only `--debug-ignored` still lists it by name, never reading it. Tests:
`git_negations_never_list_or_read_git` in `crates/dctx/tests/git_and_symlink_privacy.rs` and in the pack snapshot.

### Symlinks (v1)
`dctx::FsSource` never follows a symlink: a symlinked final component is refused before the open, and the open
itself uses `O_NOFOLLOW` (raw platform values; crates/dctx has no `libc` dependency), so a symlink swapped in after
the stat is refused by the kernel; the opened handle must be a regular file. A symlinked intermediate directory is
refused for listings and reads. Tests: `crates/dctx/src/adapters/fs.rs` and `crates/dctx/tests/git_and_symlink_privacy.rs`.

### `DCTX_INDEX_IGNORED=1`
This environment switch (dctx-cli `host::project_rules`) makes `pack` and the map verbs ignore every ignore file
(global ignore, `.gitignore`, nested `.gitignore`, `.dctxignore`); omit files and the built-in rules still load.
It does not touch the SENSITIVE deny, the `.git` guard or the symlink rules above: those do not come from rule
files. `<repo>/scripts/checks/V1-1.zsh` reruns its canary checks with the switch set.

---

## Privacy Guarantees (Formal)

### Guarantee 1: Ignored Files Never Enter Read Queue ✅
**Assertion:** Files matching ignore rules are excluded at tree construction time (`walker.rs:136-146`) via `should_ignore_item()` check. They never appear in the `DirContextTreeNode` tree, therefore never collected by `collect_file_paths()`, therefore never read by `populate_file_contents_parallel()`.

**Verification:** ✅ PROVEN
- ✅ Static code analysis completed (WO-052)
- ✅ Unit test: `test_collect_file_paths_skips_ignored` - ignored file never in read queue
- ✅ Unit test: `test_collect_file_paths_skips_ignored_subtree` - entire subtrees skipped
- ✅ Privacy guarantee formally proven through test chain

### Guarantee 2: Ignored Folders Skip Recursion
**Assertion:** When a folder matches ignore rules, `walk_recursive()` uses `continue` (walker.rs:146) to skip the item entirely. The function is never called recursively on that folder's children.

**Verification:**
- Performance benchmark: 500MB `node_modules/` should take < 100ms to skip
- Without ignore: Same folder would take 5-10 seconds to scan
- Debug mode exception: Recurses but still never reads files

### Guarantee 3: Debug Mode Does Not Compromise Privacy ✅
**Assertion:** When `--debug-ignored` is active, the system recurses into ignored folders and shows them in the tree, but the files are marked with `is_ignored: true` flag. The `populate_file_contents_parallel()` function respects this flag and never calls `fs::read()` on ignored files.

**Verification:** ✅ PROVEN
- ✅ Test: `test_ignored_files_shown_with_marker` - `.env` appears in tree with [IGNORED]
- ✅ Test: `test_ignored_files_never_have_content` - no content blocks for ignored files
- ✅ Test: `test_collect_file_paths_skips_ignored` - ignored files never enter read queue
- ✅ Privacy preserved even in debug mode (WO-051, WO-052, WO-053)

### Guarantee 4: Template Variables Cannot Trigger Unsafe Reads ✅
**Assertion:** Template variables are classified by I/O requirement:
- **Metadata-Only:** `{{{file_id}}}`, `{{{file_path}}}`, `{{{file_size}}}`, `{{{mod}}}` (safe - from `stat()`)
- **Content-Requiring:** `{{{lines}}}`, `{{{content_preview}}}` (unsafe - requires `fs::read()`)

For ignored/omitted files, content-requiring variables are never resolved due to `!node.is_ignored` guard preventing content block rendering.

**Verification:** ✅ PROVEN
- ✅ Test: `test_template_variable_safety_for_ignored_files` with 6 comprehensive assertions (WO-054)
- ✅ Documentation: Module-level safety documentation in llm_formatter.rs
- ✅ Documentation: Template Variable Safety section in DEVELOPER-GUIDE.md
- ✅ Multi-layer defense prevents any code path from triggering reads on ignored files

---

## Performance Characteristics

### Ignored Folder Skip (Primary Optimization)
**Scenario:** Project with 500MB `node_modules/` (50,000 files)

| Mode | Behavior | Time | `fs::read()` Calls |
|------|----------|------|-------------------|
| Default | Skip entire folder | < 100ms | 0 |
| Without ignore | Scan all 50k files | 5-10 sec | 50,000 |
| Debug mode | Recurse but don't read | < 500ms | 0 |

**Performance Gain:** 50-100x faster for large ignored folders.

### Omit Pattern Performance
**Scenario:** Lockfiles in monorepo (20 files, 10MB each)

| Mode | Behavior | Time | Memory |
|------|----------|------|--------|
| Include all | Read all lockfiles | ~200ms | 200MB |
| Omit lockfiles | Show in tree, skip content | ~10ms | 2MB |

**Performance Gain:** 20x faster, 100x less memory.

---

url: https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/templates-contract/
title: Template contract (DTS v2)
source: https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/docs/design/contracts/DTS-v2.md
---

# DTS source v2 and compiled plan IR v1

DX-A0b · versioned contract sketch · not final new source syntax.
Defines organization control of every mode under the accepted structure.
Depends on API/identity/parser contracts; used by B2/D1 and all mode engines.
Preserves the v1 compiler/rendering contract while extending typed policy.

## Compatibility and typed plan

DTS v1 variables, partials, layouts, four marker definitions, static resolution
and runtime data injection remain valid with byte-identical fixture outputs.
A version declaration selects v2; never infer version by an unknown field.
Legacy defaults compile to an explicit pack plan. Every map/future mode request
also receives a compiled default/custom plan; there is no second hidden policy
language or engine path bypassing DTS.

```text
ContextPlanV1 = {
  source_language_version, ir_major:1, ir_minor:0,
  required_capabilities, selection_rules, extraction_rules,
  budget_rules, views, render_program,
  selection_digest, extraction_digest, render_digest, plan_digest
}
```

| Typed section | Responsibility | Validation |
|---|---|---|
| SELECT | Paths/languages/kinds and Include/Exclude/OmitContent/DebugVisible policy | Root-relative paths, bounded rule count, no grant expansion |
| INDEX | Requested facts, parser/dialect, extraction limits | Available parser capability; Rust default `syn`; optional native only explicit |
| BUDGET | Final bytes/estimated tokens, records/depth, parse/memory/work bounds | Nonnegative bounded quantities; intersect host/mode ceilings; overflow refused |
| VIEW | Pack/map/future projection naming selection/extraction/budget/render refs | All references resolved, acyclic, mode capability present |
| RENDER | Existing partials/layout/markers plus bounded record iteration | No arbitrary evaluation, filesystem/network/process access or loaded plugins |

Source examples in proposal §2 are illustrative; B2 freezes precise grammar
and source fixtures before parser implementation. The typed semantics above
are normative. Custom source is built with explicit `template build`; shipped
compiled defaults need no runtime source parse. Template *sources* remain
user-owned; compiled plans are reconstructible cache entries.

## Permission and budgets

`permission = host_grant ∩ organization_ceiling ∩ session_selection`.
Within that ceiling, preserve existing ordered last-match ignore/omit semantics.
A template can narrow access but never turn a host denial into Include.
DebugVisible authorizes metadata only. Read rule/config sources through explicit
capabilities; unreadable policy is `PolicyUnavailable`, never default-allow.
Compiled plans bind their policy inputs/revision; changed/removed policy sources
invalidate authorization before cached facts or render output can be served.

Selection/extraction digests change index validity independently. Rendering-only
changes do not reparse source; they still change the plan/render digest and
continuation compatibility. A parser capability/revision change alters FactKey.
Budget/depth narrowing cannot make previously unauthorized facts visible.

Final-output token estimate is `ceil(2 * UTF8_bytes / 7)` over the complete
encoded answer. Rendering reserves headers, delimiters, escaping and continuation
before choosing whole records. Loops traverse only authorized records under
iteration/work bounds. Cyclic partials, unknown variables/opcodes, missing
capabilities and impossible envelopes are typed errors; no fallback rendering
that violates the configured mode or privacy ceiling.

## Compiled IR envelope

IR magic `DCTXIR\0\0` (8 bytes), major/minor u16, exact total length u64,
required capability bitset u64, section_count u32, followed by bounded typed
sections. Each section has `kind:u16, schema:u16, length:u32, payload[length]`.
Trailing SHA-256 covers all preceding bytes. Integer encoding is little-endian;
strings have checked u32 byte lengths and UTF-8. Maximum plan 1 MiB, 64 sections,
10,000 instructions; caller may narrow. Unknown required section/opcode/version
refuses load. No native-memory layout or executable serialized pointers.

Canonical sections order SELECT/INDEX/BUDGET/VIEW/RENDER/provenance, sorted named
definitions with source rule order preserved inside each. Domain-separated
identity framing (identity v1 kind 8) defines plan_digest; render_digest uses
kind 8 with a distinct IR schema/domain payload identifying render-only input.
Selection uses kind 4, extraction kind 5. B2 supplies canonical encoding goldens
and corruption fuzzing before compiled IR is a release format.

## Owner tests and model

B2 owns v1 parity, v2 compile/load determinism, section/opcode rejection and
positive controls; P1 authorization-before-render, P5 final budget, P6 frozen
clock/reordered-input equality. Model compile→validated-plan→authorized-view→
bounded-render transitions and policy-epoch revocation. Mutation removing the
host intersection must fail a denied-content test. Mutation budgeting unescaped
strings must fail a Unicode/JSON envelope property. Unsupported parser tests
include a positive `syn` capability case and explicit optional tree-sitter case.
Future modes must add their typed VIEW capability and conformance fixture to
this same compiler/facade contract before release.

url: https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/templating/
title: Templating engine (ADR-003)
source: https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/docs/ADR-003-Templating-Engine.md
---

# ADR-003: Extensible Templating System (DTS) & Compilation Strategy

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-01-08
**Author:** dctx Team
**Context:** Users require granular control over the output format to support various AI models. The system must maintain high performance (avoiding expensive parsing on every run) and ensure robustness (instructions matching output).

## 1. Decision: Explicit Marker Definition
To ensure future compatibility with non-HTML-like syntax, the templating language separates "Opening" and "Closing" logic for tags into four distinct definitions:
*   `start_marker_open` (Default: `<`)
*   `start_marker_close` (Default: `>`)
*   `end_marker_open` (Default: `</`)
*   `end_marker_close` (Default: `>`)

This allows users to redefine tags completely, e.g., to `[SECTION]` ... `[/SECTION]` or `{{#SECTION}}` ... `{{/SECTION}}`.

## 2. Decision: "Ahead-of-Time" (AOT) Template Compilation
Parsing text templates, validating variable references, and checking for cycles is expensive. We will **not** do this during the standard `dctx` runtime.

### The "Baked-In" Default
The default template (defined in the ADR) is parsed at **Rust Compile Time** (or hardcoded as a static struct). This ensures `dctx` runs with zero parsing overhead out-of-the-box.

### User Custom Templates
Users can edit templates in `~/.config/dctx/templates/`. However, `dctx` does not read these text files directly during snapshot generation.
*   **Action:** User edits `.dctx_template` file.
*   **Command:** User runs `dctx template build <path>`.
*   **Process:**
    1.  `dctx` parses the text file.
    2.  Validates syntax and variable references.
    3.  Serializes the parsed structure into an optimized binary format (e.g., `bincode`).
    4.  Saves the result to `~/.cache/dctx/templates/user_custom.bin`.
*   **Runtime:** When `dctx` runs, if configured to use a custom template, it loads this pre-validated binary directly into memory.

## 3. Decision: Two-Pass Rendering Engine
The rendering engine operates in two distinct passes to separate Configuration from Data.

*   **Pass 1 (Config Resolution):** Occurs during the "Template Build" phase. Resolves all `{{VAR}}` placeholders within the `[VARIABLES]` section.
*   **Pass 2 (Data Injection):** Occurs during runtime. Injects `{{{DATA}}}` into the pre-compiled Partial structures (`[PARTIALS]` section) and assembles the `[LAYOUT]`.

## 4. Template File Structure
The file format uses a custom INI-like syntax with three specific sections:
1.  **[VARIABLES]:** Key-Value pairs for static strings.
2.  **[PARTIALS]:** Definitions for repeated elements (`TREE_ENTRY`, `FILE_BLOCK`).
3.  **[LAYOUT]:** The global document structure.

## 5. Available Data Variables (Runtime)
These variables are populated by the Rust core:
*   `{{{node.id}}}`: Optimized incremental ID (e.g., 1, 2, 10).
*   `{{{node.path}}}`: Relative path.
*   `{{{node.type_char}}}`: `[D]` or `[F]`.
*   `{{{node.mod}}}`: Unix timestamp in milliseconds. Available to custom templates. The built-in default template does not print it since 1.0.1, because a timestamp changes on a bare `touch` and breaks the byte-stable prefix of the page; `--tree-stamps=on` selects the built-in stamped template (the 1.0.0 text, `MOD:` and `SIZE:` on every tree line, `MOD` in the instructions). The default entry also leaves out `{{{node.size_part}}}`, since a size changes on every ordinary edit; `{{{node.size}}}` and `{{{node.size_part}}}` stay available to custom templates.
*   `{{{node.size}}}`: File size in bytes.
*   `{{{file.lines}}}`: Line count of the file.
*   `{{{file.content}}}`: Actual file content.



6. TEMPLATE DEFINITION V1:

```text
# ==============================================================================
# DCTX TEMPLATE DEFINITION V1
# ==============================================================================
# This file defines how the LLM context is formatted.
# It consists of three sections: [VARIABLES], [PARTIALS], and [LAYOUT].
#
# SYNTAX GUIDE:
# - {{VAR_NAME}}      : Inserts a configuration variable defined in [VARIABLES].
# - {{{DATA_FIELD}}}  : Inserts dynamic data from the project (e.g., file content).
#
# ==============================================================================

[VARIABLES]
# --- 1. Syntactic Markers (Granular Control) ---
# Defines the exact characters used to wrap tags.
# Allows handling XML, HTML, or Custom formats safely.
start_marker_open  = "<"
start_marker_close = ">"
end_marker_open    = "</"
end_marker_close   = ">"

# --- 2. Semantic Marker Names ---
# Defines the keywords used inside the tags.
instr_marker         = "INSTRUCTIONS"
tree_start_marker    = "DIRECTORY_TREE"
tree_end_marker      = "DIRECTORY_TREE"
file_start_marker    = "FILE_CONTENT_START"
file_end_marker      = "FILE_CONTENT_END"

# --- 3. Attribute Keys ---
# Used inside tags to denote properties.
attr_id    = "ID"
attr_path  = "PATH"
attr_size  = "SIZE"
attr_lines = "LINES"
attr_mod   = "MOD"

# --- 4. Instructions Block Text ---
# This text explains the format to the LLM. It references the variables above
# to ensure the instructions always match the actual format used.
# Use '\n' for new lines.
instructions_text = "1. Manifest: The {{start_marker_open}}{{tree_start_marker}}{{start_marker_close}} section lists all files.\n   - Each entry: [TYPE] RELATIVE_PATH ({{attr_id}}:UNIQUE_ID)\n   - TYPE is [D] for directory, [F] for file.\n2. Content Access: To read a specific file:\n   - Find its UNIQUE_ID from the directory tree.\n   - Search for the marker: {{start_marker_open}}{{file_start_marker}} {{attr_id}}=\"UNIQUE_ID\"{{start_marker_close}}\n   - The content is between this marker and {{end_marker_open}}{{file_end_marker}} {{attr_id}}=\"UNIQUE_ID\"{{end_marker_close}}"

# ==============================================================================
# [PARTIALS]
# Defines the look of repeated elements (Tree items and Files).
# ==============================================================================

# --- Tree Entry Partial ---
# Context: 'node' object
# Available Data: {{{node.type_char}}}, {{{node.path}}}, {{{node.id}}}, {{{node.mod}}}, {{{node.size}}}
# The default entry leaves {{{node.mod}}} and {{{node.size_part}}} out (1.0.1); a custom template may add `, {{attr_mod}}:{{{node.mod}}}{{{node.size_part}}}`.
[PARTIAL:TREE_ENTRY]
{{{node.type_char}}} {{{node.path}}} ({{attr_id}}:{{{node.id}}})

# --- File Block Partial ---
# Context: 'file' object
# Available Data: {{{file.id}}}, {{{file.path}}}, {{{file.lines}}}, {{{file.size}}}, {{{file.content}}}
[PARTIAL:FILE_BLOCK]
{{start_marker_open}}{{file_start_marker}} {{attr_id}}="{{{file.id}}}" {{attr_path}}="{{{file.path}}}" {{attr_size}}="{{{file.size}}}" {{attr_lines}}="{{{file.lines}}}"{{start_marker_close}}
{{{file.content}}}
{{end_marker_open}}{{file_end_marker}} {{attr_id}}="{{{file.id}}}"{{end_marker_close}}

# ==============================================================================
# [LAYOUT]
# The master structure of the final output file.
# Note: The Version Header (e.g. [DCTX_SNAPSHOT_V1]) is hardcoded in the binary
# and NOT included here.
# ==============================================================================
[LAYOUT]
{{start_marker_open}}{{instr_marker}}{{start_marker_close}}
{{instructions_text}}
{{end_marker_open}}{{instr_marker}}{{end_marker_close}}

{{start_marker_open}}{{tree_start_marker}}{{start_marker_close}}
{{{comp.tree}}}
{{end_marker_open}}{{tree_end_marker}}{{end_marker_close}}

{{{comp.files}}}
```

---
url: https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/language-coverage/
title: Language coverage (ADR-018)
source: https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/docs/ADR-018-Language-Coverage.md
---

# ADR-018: Language Coverage

**Status:** accepted (PA, decision 114, pending the maintainer confirmation)

## Context

### The Problem

Map facts need explicit coverage and completion claims across source/configuration languages; precision is separate from edge confidence (`crates/dctx-map-model/src/domain/precision.rs`).

### Root Cause Analysis

Structural extraction is not a full grammar claim, and incomplete extraction must not silently become complete facts (`crates/dctx-map-model/src/domain/precision.rs`, `crates/dctx-map-parse/src/adapters/mod.rs`).

## Decision

Use pure structural extraction for 13 families: Rust, JavaScript/TypeScript, Markdown, Python, Go, Java, C/C++, configuration (JSON/TOML/YAML), C#, Kotlin, Ruby, PHP and Swift (`crates/dctx/src/index/extract.rs`, `docs/CRATE-MAP.md`).

The facade's default profile uses hand-written extraction, including line-oriented Rust and the first-party Markdown extractor. **Qualification:** `dctx-lex-rust` itself uses `syn`; it is optional behind facade `syntax-rust`, so “13 hand-written lexers” is not a claim about every lexer crate or map-parse Rust implementation (`crates/dctx/src/index/extract.rs`, `crates/dctx/Cargo.toml`, `crates/dctx-lex-rust/src/lib.rs`).

Keep one shared facade dispatch and fact-to-symbol conversion in `crates/dctx/src/index/lex_dispatch.rs`; Rust and Markdown retain specialized entry paths in `crates/dctx/src/index/extract.rs`.

Carry coverage (`syntax`, `structural`, `opaque`), completion (`complete`, `partial`, `refused`) and bounded parser identity separately from confidence (`crates/dctx-map-model/src/domain/precision.rs`).

## Implementation

### Phase 1: Pure Lexers and Facade Projection

The shared dispatch converts nodes without reading source or retaining bodies. New language branches expose only complete extraction; JavaScript/TypeScript preserve their existing partial-fact projection (`crates/dctx/src/index/lex_dispatch.rs`).

The facade rejects NUL/non-UTF-8 symbol extraction and assigns stable ids and containment after extraction (`crates/dctx/src/index/extract.rs`).

### Phase 2: Map-parse Adapters

`PureParser` dispatches the language adapters over caller-provided bytes; partial/diagnostic extraction is refused as `ParseError::Syntax`, and unknown languages have a module-only fallback (`crates/dctx-map-parse/src/adapters/mod.rs`).

Shared fact assembly records file precision and finalizes source-ordered facts with duplicate-id handling (`crates/dctx-map-parse/src/adapters/facts.rs`).

### Phase 3: Store Invariants Gate

The parser gate checks file ownership, unique/kind-correct ids, source-bounded spans, valid confidence/kind combinations, existing edge endpoints and containment reachability. It also simulates query insertion of Place/Package nodes to catch duplicate ids (`crates/dctx-map-parse/tests/lexers.rs`, `crates/dctx-map-parse/tests/fuzz_all.rs`).

### Phase 4: Fuzz Gate

Seeded bounded property tests exercise arbitrary bytes, Unicode, malformed inputs, deterministic results, successful-result store invariants and fixture prefixes without executing source (`crates/dctx-map-parse/tests/fuzz_all.rs`).

## Results

The gate source defines successful fixture controls as well as refusal/robustness cases; this record asserts test obligations, not a new passing execution (`crates/dctx-map-parse/tests/lexers.rs`, `crates/dctx-map-parse/tests/fuzz_all.rs`).

## Trade-offs

### Benefits

Structural facts can be produced without a default tree-sitter runtime, with explicit precision and conservative abstention (`crates/dctx-map-parse/src/adapters/mod.rs`, `crates/dctx/src/index/lex_dispatch.rs`).

### Costs

The facade's structural Rust profile and optional syn path differ; the shared facade dispatch also deliberately differs from PureParser on JavaScript partial facts (`crates/dctx/src/index/extract.rs`, `crates/dctx/src/index/lex_dispatch.rs`, `crates/dctx-map-parse/src/adapters/mod.rs`).

## Alternatives Considered

The earlier spec proposed tree-sitter as the parser dependency. Current adapters retain it only behind `syntax-tree-sitter` as an optional oracle; languages without an included grammar use pure adapters even in that oracle (`docs/SPEC-MAP-MODE.md`, `crates/dctx-map-parse/src/adapters/mod.rs`).

## References

Inventory: `docs/CRATE-MAP.md`; facade: `crates/dctx/src/index/lex_dispatch.rs`; adapters: `crates/dctx-map-parse/src/adapters/mod.rs`; robustness: `crates/dctx-map-parse/tests/fuzz_all.rs`.

## Lessons Learned

Language family count, structural coverage, grammar completeness and edge confidence are distinct claims; the Rust implementation qualification must remain visible (`docs/CRATE-MAP.md`, `crates/dctx-map-model/src/domain/precision.rs`, `crates/dctx-lex-rust/src/lib.rs`).

## Future Work

Keep tree-sitter optional and preserve precision/refusal and store-invariant gates when extending adapters; optional oracle coverage is limited to its included grammars (`crates/dctx-map-parse/src/adapters/mod.rs`, `crates/dctx-map-parse/tests/fuzz_all.rs`).

title: Three-way benchmark
source: https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/docs/BENCHMARK-20261030.md
---

# dctx vs Trail-Code vs graphify: three-way benchmark (30 October 2026)

One command, same host, same corpora, same CPU set, no network, pinned versions. Raw aggregate, headline tables
and the harness are in [`research/bench-3way-20261030/`](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/tree/main/docs/research/bench-3way-20261030); the gap analysis behind
the work is `GAP-MATRIX-20261030.md`. Where another tool wins, the tables say so.

- **dctx**: `main` at `ac8408c` (the following commit only changes `CHANGELOG.md`), release build,
  sha256 `82bd48760932305748a00d2b32901c667af948f602822b9816cc5c545de7ebbc`.
  Baseline for "before" columns: `main` at `4660f6d`, the state before this night's work.
- **Trail-Code** `@trailhq/trail-code` 0.28.0 from npm, `trail build .` (no `--deep`, no `--lsp`).
- **graphify** `graphifyy` 0.9.97 from PyPI, LLM-free code path only (`extract --code-only`,
  `GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none`). Its LLM pass over docs, PDFs and images was **not** run, and nothing here measures it.

## Headline

| Area | Result |
|---|---|
| Task-level questions, October protocol (70 questions) | **Run 7: dctx 140 of 140, Trail-Code 122, graphify 96**, with dctx using 29.3k tokens against Trail-Code's 88.9k and graphify's 197k. See "Run 7" below. |
| Callers (depth 1) against a tool-independent gold set, 80 targets on 4 corpora | **Run 5: dctx P 0.995 / R 0.851 (first page), R 0.968 following 5 pages.** Run 1 below: dctx P 0.993 / R 0.461 (first page), P 0.995 / R 0.706 following up to 5 pages. Trail-Code P 0.986 / R 0.436, graphify P 0.989 / R 0.196. Per corpus, Trail-Code wins ripgrep and trailcode, and dctx wins flask and pocketbase. Before tonight dctx recall was 0. |
| Cold index | **dctx fastest on all 6 corpora**: 0.16–1.16 s against 1.17–58.3 s for Trail-Code and 4.5–59 s for graphify. Peak RSS 19–90 MB against 121–1,020 MB and 74–394 MB. |
| Warm queries (median of 5, including process start) | **dctx fastest** on search, callers and skeleton everywhere: 44–226 ms against 0.98–1.9 s for Trail-Code and 0.38–1.4 s for graphify. graphify's overview is a 7 ms read of a pre-written file. |
| Answer size | dctx `map hubs` gives the smallest overview on 4 of 6 corpora (Trail-Code on trailcode and docs) (30–652 tokens; Trail-Code 18–2,538; graphify 3,827–11,591). graphify gives the smallest callers and skeleton answers. dctx's skeleton is the largest of the three on ripgrep (1,784 tokens). Before tonight dctx's only overview was a 0.45–2.6 M-token `pack`. |
| Cache-friendliness | dctx and Trail-Code tie. Both are byte-identical across runs, and after an unrelated edit only the overview changes. graphify changed find, skeleton and overview after `update`, and 1 of 6 ripgrep queries was not deterministic. |
| Network | dctx and graphify made 0 socket attempts in every variant. Trail-Code made 49 blocked connect attempts when `DO_NOT_TRACK` is unset, and 0 with it set. |
| Language coverage, mixed corpus (10 languages) | **Symbols: dctx 10 of 10, Trail-Code 7, graphify 5.** **Call edges, run 3: dctx 10 of 10, Trail-Code 7, graphify 5** (run 1: dctx 0). dctx's new outline tier is symbols only, labelled `guess`. Terraform and SQL get symbols only from dctx. |
| Plain-text docs (.md/.rst/.txt/.adoc corpus) | dctx indexes the corpus into headed sections (0.18 s). graphify's code-only mode produced no index, and Trail-Code indexes no doc nodes. |
| Privacy canary (git-tracked `.env` files) | Run 3: **clean for all three tools** (DCX-30). Run 1: **dctx still leaked on one path.** `pack`, `find` and `grep` are clean now; before tonight `pack` printed the canary. But an explicit `dctx map read m:.env` returns the file. Trail-Code and graphify leaked nothing. The fix is card DCX-30, which has not landed. |

## Run 7: 140 of 140 (main `53f8b6b`, 31 October, 06:20 UTC)

New since run 6:
- DCX-54c: `neighbors --dir out` also lists the calls the index cannot resolve, as `calls:out:?<name>` records after the resolved callees. These are receiver methods, builtins and external package calls.
- DCX-56b: dotted config key matching (`dotted_key`), not yet wired into `find`.
- DCX-61: PowerShell symbols and command-position call edges.

All landed checks passed together on the Linux benchmark host before the run. Raw results are in `research/bench-3way-20261030/tasks/results/run5-53f8b6b/` and `research/bench-3way-20261030/results/run7-53f8b6b/`.

**Task-level protocol** (70 questions, 354 gold facts; generator, mapping and scorer unchanged):

| Tool | Points /140 | Gold facts /354 | Tokens | Facts per 1k tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| dctx `53f8b6b` | **140** (run 6: 136) | **353** (342) | **29,340** | **12.0** |
| Trail-Code 0.28.0 | 122 | 312 | 88,923 | 3.51 |
| graphify 0.9.97, code-only | 96 | 238 | 197,203 | 1.21 |

dctx scores every point on all ten question types. Callees went from 10 to 14 of 14 (37 of 38 facts). It uses a third of Trail-Code's tokens and a seventh of graphify's.

**Three-way run 7**: callers P / R on the first page 0.995 / 0.851 (all pages 0.968), the same as run 6. The language coverage table is unchanged at 10 of 10 with symbols and 9 of 10 with call edges; shell is still `n`. Its per-language edge counts rise (for example Scala 1 to 8) because the probe counts every `calls` record, and since DCX-54c that includes the `calls:out:?` names. A count above zero says nothing new about resolved edges, so this run does not claim more resolved edges.

## Run 6 (main `82ec474`, 31 October, 02:04 UTC)

New since run 5:
- DCX-57: a declaration-only symbol (`.mli`, C/C++ header, `.d.ts`) answers neighbors for its paired definition.
- DCX-64: Erlang (not in the mixed corpus).
- DCX-55b and DCX-54b: `export_list` and `out_calls`, which are not yet wired into answers.

All landed checks plus these four passed together on the Linux benchmark host before the run. Raw results are in `research/bench-3way-20261030/results/run6-82ec474/` and `research/bench-3way-20261030/tasks/results/run4-82ec474/`.

- Call-edge coverage on the mixed corpus: **9 of 10** (run 5: 8). OCaml now has edges through the `.mli` pairing. Shell still has none, because the probe samples bats `@test` blocks that call only external commands. Trail-Code has 7 and graphify 5.
- Callers P / R, first page: 0.995 / 0.851, unchanged (all pages 0.968).
- Task protocol: **136 / 140**, unchanged. Trail-Code has 122 and graphify 96. The 4 lost points are still callees questions; card DCX-54c wires `out_calls` into neighbors.

## Latest: run 5 and task-level re-run 3 (main `a906884`, 30 October, 16:39 and 17:05 UTC)

dctx `a906884` adds four cards on top of run 4. DCX-50 spreads callers over files, makes bare calls skip methods, and ranks data-file keys below code. DCX-51 puts exported declarations first in outlines, gives read sites for config keys, adds line numbers to find, and ranks exact-word concepts first. DCX-52 orders callers by call-site count and fits pages to the budget. DCX-53 adds deeper Scala, Zig, Lua, Elixir and OCaml symbols. All 36 landed checks passed together on the Linux benchmark host before the run. The binary's sha256 starts with `76d8e9b59821`. dctx leads or ties on every type. The 4 points it still loses are all callees questions: ripgrep, pocketbase, django and core lose 1 each. In the three public corpora every missing fact is a call that the index could not resolve: a receiver method (`line_terminator`, `lookup_allowed`), a builtin (`callable`) or an external package (`Validate`). The core rows are sanitized. Card DCX-54 lists these calls.

Call-edge coverage on the mixed corpus is **8 of 10** by the probe; Trail-Code has 7 and graphify 5. The probe samples the first 25 symbols of the six largest files per language. It now follows every skeleton page, so its symbol counts are comparable with Trail-Code's full listing. Two languages miss for reasons outside the call resolver:
- OCaml: the first 25 symbols all come from `cmdliner.mli`, an interface file with no bodies. On `cmdliner_arg.ml` itself, `str_of_pp` lists 3 callers with their call lines. Card DCX-57 makes an interface declaration answer for its definition.
- Shell: the first 25 symbols are bats `@test` blocks in `test/bats.bats`, which call external commands only.

This is the same protocol as October: 70 questions over seven corpora, 354 gold facts, and October's generator and scorer. **Trail-Code still wins the task-level test.** dctx gained 8 points and needs a fifth of October's tokens, because its overview question now uses `map hubs` instead of the unbounded legacy tree. dctx's answers are the densest: 7.5 facts per 1,000 tokens against Trail-Code's 3.5. Where dctx still loses:
- Caller facts need the call line, and `neighbors` returns the calling function's span.
- Config-key and concept questions score 0 under the October mapping.
- A supplementary run that uses the verbs added since October reached 96 points (`map grep` for config keys, `map skeleton` for outlines). It is not the October protocol, so it is not counted above.

## Method

- Host: a Linux benchmark host (Debian 13, Xeon E5-2680 v2), shared with other jobs. Load was 3.2 at the start, so absolute
  latencies are noisy. Every measured command ran as `nice -n 10 taskset -c 24-31 unshare -Urn env -i …`, with no
  network, scratch HOME and caches, and `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`. One heavy process ran at a time. The network audit is a
  ptrace socket tracer, because strace is not installed.
- Corpora are pinned by SHA in `research/bench-3way-20261030/corpora-shas.json`: flask 3.1.3, ripgrep 15.2.0,
  pocketbase v0.40.5, Trail-Code at the 0.28.0 release commit, a mixed corpus of one public repo for each of 10
  languages, and a docs corpus built from python/devguide, rust-lang/book and asciidoctor.
- Tokens are `ceil(stdout_bytes / 3.5)` for every tool. That is an estimate, not a tokenizer.
- Cold runs use 3 repetitions, except 1 for any tool whose first run took more than 30 s (Trail-Code and graphify
  on pocketbase and trailcode). Warm runs take the median of 5 after one discarded warm-up.
- The callers gold set is the regex oracle of the October protocol (`goldlib.py`) on 20 seeded targets per corpus.
  A hit is true when its span contains a gold call site.
- Query mapping: dctx `map find` / `map neighbors --dir in --edge calls` / `map skeleton` / `map hubs`.
  Trail-Code `ask` / `callers` / `skeleton` / `map`. graphify `query` / `affected --relation calls` /
  `explain <file>` / `GRAPH_REPORT.md`.

## Not claimed

- Task-level answer quality with a frozen model. The fact-scoring protocol was re-run; Trail-Code leads it, 122 to 77.
- Anything about graphify's LLM semantic graph, or Trail-Code's learnings and LSP edges.
- SWE-bench or agent-run numbers.
- Equal language depth. dctx's 25 new formats are outline tier: symbols, not call edges.

## What changed in dctx tonight (all on `main`, not pushed)

Call and import edges (`19e90a1`), byte-stable answers (`ce18608`), `.env` omission in pack (`6d4deec`),
outline symbols for 25 formats and plain-text sections (`9c61ac9`, `e0821e3`, `839bd45`, `a32dad3`),
neighbors depth 4 (`0de5ce1`), `hubs` (`6bc0cbc`), `grep` (`5691234`), `skeleton` (`2243c38`), `path` (`670e9e3`),
`export` (`ac8408c`), `dctx mcp` (`50bbce4`) and a 1 GiB source ceiling (`5d26781`). Every card's own check, and
then all 15 checks together on `ac8408c`, passed on the Linux benchmark host before the benchmark ran.

## Next

1. DCX-30: map mode must never serve env-shaped files. This is the remaining privacy leak.
2. Call edges for the outline tier, to close the 0-of-10 call-edge coverage on the mixed corpus.
3. Recall on ripgrep and trailcode (0.25 and 0.33 against Trail-Code's 0.33 and 0.90): method calls through
   receivers and re-exports.
4. Re-run the 70-question task protocol with a frozen model.

## Independent benchmark (v1 card 6), 31.10.2026, run uncapped on the Linux benchmark host

Seeded selection of 3 repos the tools never saw (zoxide, requests, gin), gold from language servers and repo history, published regardless of outcome. Tasks: dctx 22/28 points, 31/36 facts, 6.85 facts per 1k tokens (Trail-Code 19/28, graphify 14/28). Callers against LSP gold, first page: dctx P 0.730 / R 0.341, Trail-Code P 0.731 / R 0.313, graphify P 0.920 / R 0.264. Honest read: dctx leads on task answers and token efficiency; caller recall on unseen repos is far below the in-house corpus (0.851), so the caller floors above hold only for the curated corpora. Full table and raw JSON: `docs/research/bench-independent/results/20261031T191225Z/`.

# STAB-01: byte stability on `0495f5f`

Measured **2026-11-06 UTC** on Linux from commit
`0495f5f87717df5385209d306b92328a8cd96cf6`. The directory date is the card's
requested evidence destination. No engine changes were made.

| Measurement | Text | JSON |
|---|---:|---:|
| Answers identical after unrelated edit | 33/33 | 33/33 |
| Answers identical over five separate invocations | 33/33 | 33/33 |
| Baseline → post-edit common-prefix ratio, minimum / mean | 1.0 / 1.0 | 1.0 / 1.0 |
| Consecutive same-request transitions, five per case | 165 | 165 |
| Same-request M7, minimum / mean | 1.0 / 1.0 | 1.0 / 1.0 |
| Consecutive changing-question transitions | 195 | 195 |
| Changing-question M7, minimum / median / mean | 0.007795889 / 0.107142857 / 0.214830257 | 0.008776458 / 0.067594433 / 0.182446794 |
| Changing-question M7, total prefix bytes / total current bytes | 0.061846978 | 0.079892615 |

All **405 CLI invocations exited 0**, with empty stderr: 396 measurement invocations
(66 cases × six runs), three target-resolution invocations, and six snapshot
controls. All 33 default text headers were exactly `# <place> <verb>`; all 33
default JSON answers omitted snapshot, generation and `freshness.age_s`.
`--meta --json` controls confirmed that each corpus's snapshot changed after the edit.

## Protocol and pins

The original producer is
[`phase_query.py`](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/docs/research/trail-code-2026-10/scripts/phase_query.py), with byte comparisons
in [`aggregate.py`](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/docs/research/trail-code-2026-10/scripts/aggregate.py), section 7. It runs
five warm queries, appends a comment to an unrelated file in another directory,
reruns queries, and restores the file. Its original evidence remains at
[`data/stability.csv`](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/docs/research/trail-code-2026-10/data/stability.csv).

The original `/path/to/workdir/dctx-vs-trail` host tree is absent. The repository contains
the scripts and historical results, but no original seven-corpus checkout set or
the host's `scripts/corpora.json`. Checked alternate `bench3` and `perf-20261101`
corpora paths were also absent. This run uses the card's fallback: three corpora
extracted exclusively from tracked files at the pinned current commit. No fetch or
network access was used. The new denominator differs from the historical 0/63;
Trail-Code's historical 59/70 was not rerun.

| Corpus | Exact tracked prefix extracted | Files | Symbol / file | Unrelated file edited |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| parser-mixed | `crates/dctx-map-parse/tests/fixtures/` | 17 | `helper`, `rust/src/support.rs` | `ts/module.ts` |
| lexer-go | `crates/dctx-lex-go/` | 19 | `Add`, `tests/fixtures/basic.go` | `src/lib.rs` |
| map-query | `crates/dctx-map-query/src/` | 30 | `render_answer_at`, `adapters/output.rs` | `domain/ranking.rs` |

Each prefix is copied in full using `git ls-tree -r --name-only <pin> -- <prefix>`
and `git show <pin>:<path>`, retaining paths relative to the prefix. Every file's
size and SHA-256, and the CLI binary SHA-256, are in [`corpora.json`](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/docs/research/stability-20261105/corpora.json).
Work copies and isolated cache/config directories live in a disposable `/tmp`
directory. The live worktree's corpus files are never edited.

The original applicable map query shapes are retained: `find --limit 10`, inbound
`neighbors --edge calls` at depths 1 and 2, outbound neighbors, `map --depth 2
--limit 40`, `read`, and `explain`. Each now runs in **both** formats. The current
bounded `skeleton`, `grep`, `hubs`, and `path` verbs add four shapes per corpus,
again in both formats: 11 × 2 × 3 = 66 cases. Stable target IDs are resolved by
`find --json --limit 40`, matching exact path and symbol. `path` tests a file's
containment edge to that symbol. `grep` is confined to the target file.

Default budgets and default output are used, without `--meta` in the measured
answers. There are five warm sweeps, separated by 1.05 seconds, then a sixth sweep
after appending exactly `\n// STAB-01 unrelated comment\n` to the named unrelated
file. The comment is outside declarations and contains none of the queried names.
It changes snapshot identity without changing the selected declarations, calls,
search hits or hub counts. Original bytes are restored in a `finally` block and
verified. Configuration and caches are isolated using `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`,
`XDG_CACHE_HOME` and `DCTX_CACHE_DIR`; inherited `DCTX_*` overrides are removed.

Every JSON case has records except outbound neighbors for the two leaf functions
`helper` and `Add`. Their empty answers are included. All three inbound-neighbor
cases have records, all paths are found, and `render_answer_at` has nine returned
outbound neighbors plus eleven more in the bounded page. No cursor pages were
followed. Whole-graph `export` has no unrelated graph input and is outside this
bounded-answer protocol. The historical legacy snapshot overview, Trail-only grep
and no-refresh shapes are outside the map-answer comparison.

## M7 and acceptance limits

For each transition, M7 = longest common **byte** prefix of previous and current
stdout / **current** stdout byte length. Both block lengths and the prefix length
are stored in [`turn-prefixes.csv`](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/docs/research/stability-20261105/turn-prefixes.csv); there are no empty blocks.
No whitespace, JSON fields, paths, timestamps or newlines are normalized.

The same-request trace is each case's five warm answers followed by its post-edit
answer: five consecutive transitions per case, 330 total. The additional
changing-question trace uses actual invocation order, separately per corpus and
format: the 11 query shapes in the order above, repeated over six sweeps; 65
transitions per stream, 390 total. Text and JSON are separate context-block streams.
These are recorded tool-answer traces, with one answer treated as one injected
block; there is no provider cache-hit or task-acceptance measurement.

The local unrelated-edit and five-run JSON gates pass. The low changing-question
ratios show why this result cannot establish §12.1's T0–T3 invariant or its recorded
tier-context M7 ≥ 0.9 gate. Tier layering remains **target**. No cross-platform,
thread-count, changed-answer-content, or full original benchmark gate is claimed.
No unrelated-edit instability was observed, so there is no instability reproducer.

The three text `read` pages actually include their selected source bodies. Text
`explain` still consists of header and id/kind/path, so §11's richer text-page
contract remains a target. Other text fields, JSON compaction and provenance-trailer
contracts were not promoted to landed by this measurement.

## Exact commands and exits

Run from `/path/to/workdir/codex/STAB-01R`:

```sh
export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$PWD/.target-stab
cargo --offline build --locked -p dctx-cli > /tmp/stab-01-build.log 2>&1
```

Exit **101**: configured `sccache` failed with `Operation not permitted`, before
compilation. A retry after `unset RUSTC_WRAPPER`, with output redirected to
`/tmp/stab-01-build-no-wrapper.log`, also exited **101**: Cargo's user config still
specified `build.rustc-wrapper = "sccache"`.

```sh
export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$PWD/.target-stab
export RUSTC_WRAPPER=
cargo --offline build --locked -p dctx-cli > /tmp/stab-01-build-direct.log 2>&1
python3 docs/research/stability-20261105/measure.py > /tmp/stab-01-measure.log 2>&1
python3 docs/research/stability-20261105/verify.py
git diff --check
```

Exits: build **0**; measurement **0**; independent raw-data audit **0**;
`git diff --check` **0**. Build logs and [`measurement.txt`](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/docs/research/stability-20261105/measurement.txt) are
preserved here. [`commands.md`](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/docs/research/stability-20261105/commands.md) lists every query shape and setup/control
command; [`runs.jsonl`](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/docs/research/stability-20261105/runs.jsonl) records all 405 exact argv arrays, shell-quoted
commands, working directories, environment overrides, exits, full stdout/stderr,
byte counts and SHA-256 hashes. `measure.py` records a fresh run only when no
`runs.jsonl` exists; use a fresh copy of the evidence directory to repeat it.

[`stability.csv`](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/docs/research/stability-20261105/stability.csv) is the new measurement. The adjacent
[`stability-original.csv`](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/docs/research/stability-20261105/stability-original.csv) is a byte-for-byte copy of the
historical CSV, SHA-256
`46b54db2fb469dc4df70eaa0bf22b458a8089f437cdee3294efe071314280266`.
Placing both here keeps all writes within the card's own set; the historical
source file was neither overwritten nor modified.
