url: https://www.dctx.internet.technology/cli/
title: CLI reference (captured help)
source: https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/tools/website/data/demo.json
---

```text
$ dctx --help
Usage: dctx [PATH] [OPTIONS]
       dctx pack [PATH] [--output PATH] [--clipboard] [--json]
       dctx pack [PATH] --for <TEXT> [--budget TOKENS]
       dctx map <map|find|neighbors|explain|read|skeleton|grep|hubs|path> [--json]
       dctx mcp [PATH]
       dctx languages [--json|--markdown]
       dctx cache status [--json] [--root PATH]
       dctx cache gc [--dry-run] [--root PATH] [--max-bytes N] [--legacy]
       dctx cache purge --root PATH [--dry-run] [--yes]
       dctx cache purge --all [--dry-run] [--yes]
       dctx cache config [auto on|off] [--max-bytes N] [--ttl-days N]
       dctx cache auto [--json]
       dctx template build <PATH> [--output PATH]
       dctx template list [--dir PATH]
       dctx plugin search|install|list|info|enable|disable|remove|update|verify
       dctx git <status|protect>

`dctx languages` lists every supported language with its tier: full (symbols and call edges), outline (symbols only) or docs (sections).
`dctx mcp` serves the map verbs as MCP tools over stdio (JSON-RPC 2.0, one message per line) for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex.
Explicit `dctx pack` writes stdout, the clipboard, or `--output`. It does not create a project text file.
`dctx pack --for <TEXT>` prints task context for an agent card instead: map find, neighbors and read of the names in TEXT, cut to `--budget` estimated tokens (default 3000).
`dctx .` remains the legacy snapshot alias and still writes its documented project text.
`dctx plugin list` and `dctx --help` do not create a project `.dctx/` directory or start a plugin.
`dctx git` routes to the bundled dctx/git plugin. It is not a Git passthrough.
Cache purge requires `--root PATH` or `--all`, and `--yes` unless `--dry-run` is set.
`dctx cache gc --legacy` reads only exports the caller already registered. It does not search the home directory.
`dctx cache config` shows the persisted policy. `auto on|off` enables auto-clean, `--max-bytes` tightens the system cap, and `--ttl-days` sets idle overlay and preview lifetime.
`dctx cache auto` prints the last auto-clean time, the bytes it reclaimed and the next due time.
pack, map, template, plugin and the TUI run one bounded auto-clean when it is due. They print nothing unless bytes were reclaimed.
`--no-auto-clean` and `DCTX_AUTO_CLEAN=0` disable that slice. `DCTX_CACHE_DIR` selects the cache root.

Snapshot Options:
  -c, --clipboard       Copy to clipboard
  -d, --diff            Output diff only (if available)
  -t, --tree            Tree-Only mode (skips file content)
  -r, --reset           Force V1 reset
  -h, --help            Show help
  -v, --version         Show version
  --verbose             With --version, also show feature and precision limits

Filter Options:
  --ext <extensions>    Only include files with these extensions
  --binary              Include binary files (excluded by default)
  --empty               Show only empty files (0 bytes)
  --non-empty           Show only non-empty files
  --large <MB>          Show only files larger than X megabytes
  --small <MB>          Show only files smaller than X megabytes
  --hidden              Show ONLY hidden files and folders (starting with .)
  --debug-ignored       Show ignored files in the tree without reading them
  -V, --debug-verbose   Show ignore decision traces
  --tree-stamps=on|off  MOD: timestamps on tree lines: off (default) keeps the output prefix stable across a touch, on = the 1.0.0 text

Template Commands:
  template build <PATH>  Compile a template through the facade
  template list          List explicit compiled plans; no home-directory scan

Examples:
  dctx .                      Legacy snapshot of the current directory
  dctx pack .                 Pack to stdout and write no project text file
  dctx pack . --output out.txt
  dctx languages --json
  dctx cache status --json
  dctx cache gc --dry-run
  dctx cache purge --root /path --dry-run
  dctx cache config auto off --max-bytes 1000000 --ttl-days 7
  dctx cache auto
  dctx template build policy.dctx_template

Feature and precision limits:
facade_version: 1.1.0
profile: enhanced
wire_version: 2
segment_version: 1
storage: buffered-segments
features: pack,map,templates,fs,segments,cache,syntax-rust
parsers: dctx-structural/2,dctx-lex-js:1,dctx-lex-md:1,dctx-lex-rust/syn-3.0.9
languages: rust,javascript,typescript,python,go,java,c,csharp,kotlin,ruby,php,swift,web,scala,dart,zig,solidity,gleam,fortran,perl,groovy,powershell,elixir,lua,ocaml,r,julia,haskell,erlang,verilog,hcl,sql,clojure,lisp,scheme,elisp,config,shell,make,docker,proto,pascal,graphql,nix,markdown,text,rst,asciidoc,org,tex
unsafe_boundary: syn-dependency
native_code: false
git: false
subprocess: none
precision: the structural extractor reports declarations, imports, headings and conservative calls.
It does not promise exact semantic calls, name or type resolution, or macro expansion.
A syntax-rust build adds syn for supported Rust syntax only, still without type checking.
token estimate: ceil(2 * UTF-8 bytes / 7) is an estimate, not a tokenizer guarantee.
cache cap: 2 GiB hard, 1.5 GiB soft watermark, 1.2 GiB eviction target.
cache ttl: idle overlays and previews 7 days, unpinned roots 30 days, staging 1 day.
auto-clean interval: 1 day.

$ dctx map --help
Usage: dctx map <map|find|neighbors|explain|read|skeleton|grep> <TARGET> [OPTIONS]
       dctx map hubs [--limit N] [--json] [--place PATH] [--budget TOKENS] [--meta]
         Most-called symbols (incoming calls and imports, 1..60 lines, default 20) and per-directory file and symbol counts. No TARGET.
       dctx map path <FROM> <TO> [--json] [--place PATH] [--budget TOKENS] [--meta]
         Shortest edge path (calls, imports, contains; either direction; at most 8 hops), one `edge:out|in<TAB>id<TAB>kind<TAB>path` line per hop, or `no path`.
       dctx map export [--format json|mermaid] [--output PATH] [--place PATH]
         The whole graph as one deterministic document (default json: nodes and edges; mermaid: a flowchart of calls and imports). No TARGET, no token cap; --output writes a file.
  TARGET                  Required. map accepts a stable id or a place-relative file.
                          skeleton takes a file (or m:<path>) and prints its declaration signatures, no bodies,
                          in source order: id, kind, L<start>-<end>, signature.
                          A file path is read as m:<path>. Omitting TARGET does not scan.
  --json                  Facade JSON v2, including the precision label
  --place PATH            Place or worktree root (default: current directory)
  --meta                  Restore the snapshot digest and generation in the text header and the snapshot, generation and age_s JSON fields.
                          Without it the answer bytes do not change across unrelated edits or time.
  --profile               Stderr stage timings and the five slowest files. DCTX_PROFILE=1 is the same switch.
  DCTX_MAX_SOURCE_BYTES   Env: total source bytes one scan may read, 1..17179869184 (default 1073741824 = 1 GiB).
  DCTX_MAX_RECORDS        Env: files, symbols and edges one index may hold, 1..100000000 (default 1000000). A bigger place is refused while it is scanned.
  DCTX_MAX_ENTRIES        Env: files and directories one scan may visit, 1..100000000 (default 100000).
  DCTX_FRESHNESS          Env: strict_live hashes every file on a warm start; the default (stamp) trusts a file whose size, mtime and inode are unchanged and older than 2 s.
  --budget TOKENS         Output tokens, 1..2000 (explain max: 1000).
                          Read with no --budget uses the 2,000-token hard cap.
  --depth N               Map: 1..3; neighbors: 1..4. Explain and read take no depth.
  --limit N               Map, find and neighbors page size. Explain and read accept only 1.
  --offset N              Refused. Pass the previous page's next value to --cursor.
  --cursor TOKEN          Opaque continuation. A stale token is rejected.
  --kind fn,type,doc      Find kinds
  --in PATH               Find or grep within a relative path
  grep LITERAL            Exhaustive literal search of indexed files, hits grouped by enclosing symbol
  -i, --ignore-case       Grep: ASCII case-insensitive match
  --edge calls,imports    Neighbor edge filter
  --dir in|out|both       Neighbor direction
  --lines A-B --full      Read those absolute source lines inside the node; full permits 400
  --rev SHA               Refused: this build does not link git
Precision: structural declarations, imports, headings and conservative calls.
Not exact semantic calls, type resolution or macro expansion.
Token estimate ceil(2 * UTF-8 bytes / 7) is not a tokenizer guarantee.
Example: dctx map find 'ignore rules' --json
Example: dctx map map crates/dctx-cli/src/lib.rs --depth 2
Example: dctx map map m:crates/dctx-cli/src/lib.rs --cursor '<next from the previous page>'
Each verb's own page and example: dctx map <verb> --help
Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 no result (an id not in the index, a binary file), 2 usage, 3 index error; see docs/CLI-EXIT-CODES.md.

$ dctx map map --help
Usage: dctx map map <TARGET> [--depth 1..3] [--limit N] [--cursor TOKEN] [--json] [--place PATH] [--meta]
  Outline of a file (m:<path> or a place-relative path) or a symbol and what it contains.
Example: dctx map map src/lib.rs --depth 2

$ dctx languages --help
Usage: dctx languages [--json | --markdown]

Lists every language the map index recognises: name, tag, file names, tier and symbol confidence.
Tiers: full = symbols and call edges (lexical, not type-resolved); outline = symbols only, no call edges promised;
docs = headed sections. Confidence `guess` marks heuristic outlines, whose records carry confidence `guess`.

Options:
  --json        One JSON document with the tiers and the languages
  --markdown    The README language table
  -h, --help    Show this help

Example: dctx languages --json
```

### dctx --version

exit 0, 23 bytes, ~7 est. tokens

```text
dctx 1.1.0 (<git sha>)
```

### dctx pack .

exit 0, 5601 bytes, ~1601 est. tokens

```text
[DCTX_LLM_CONTEXT_SNAPSHOT_V1]
[DIRECTORY:kiosk]
<INSTRUCTIONS>
1. Manifest: The <DIRECTORY_TREE> section lists all files.
   - Each entry: [TYPE] RELATIVE_PATH (ID:UNIQUE_ID)
   - TYPE is [D] for directory, [F] for file.
2. Content Access: To read a specific file:
   - Find its UNIQUE_ID from the directory tree.
   - Search for the marker: <FILE_CONTENT_START ID=\"UNIQUE_ID\">
   - The content is between this marker and </FILE_CONTENT_END ID=\"UNIQUE_ID\">
</INSTRUCTIONS>
<DIRECTORY_TREE>
[D]  (ID:ROOT)
  [F] .env (ID:F001)
  [F] .gitignore (ID:F002)
  [F] Cargo.toml (ID:F003)
  [F] README.md (ID:F004)
  [F] config.toml (ID:F005)
  [D] src (ID:D006)
    [F] src/main.rs (ID:F007)
    [F] src/store.rs (ID:F008)
    [F] src/util.rs (ID:F009)
  [D] tools (ID:D010)
    [F] tools/report.py (ID:F011)
  [D] web (ID:D012)
    [F] web/app.ts (ID:F013)
    [F] web/format.ts (ID:F014)
</DIRECTORY_TREE>
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F001" PATH=".env" LINES="0">
[Content omitted by pattern rules]
</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F001">
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F002" PATH=".gitignore" LINES="2">
target/

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F002">
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F003" PATH="Cargo.toml" LINES="9">
[package]
name = "kiosk"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
description = "A tiny order kiosk: the sample project for the dctx website examples."
license = "Apache-2.0"

[dependencies]

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F003">
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F004" PATH="README.md" LINES="19">
# kiosk

A tiny order kiosk. It is the example project that every command on the dctx website runs on.

## Run

    cargo run -- ada

prints `Hello, Ada!` and saves order 1 to `orders/1.tsv`.

## Orders

Each order is one tab-separated line: id, item, quantity and a checksum of the item name.
`python3 tools/report.py orders/` sums the quantities.

## Configuration

`config.toml` holds the currency and the screen title. Secrets live in `.env`, which is never committed.

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F004">
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F005" PATH="config.toml" LINES="7">
[screen]
title = "kiosk example"
currency = "EUR"

[orders]
folder = "orders"

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F005">
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F007" PATH="src/main.rs" LINES="11">
//! kiosk: greet a customer, take one order, save it.
mod store;
mod util;

fn main() {
    let name = std::env::args().nth(1).unwrap_or_else(|| "guest".to_string());
    println!("{}", util::greet(&name));
    let order = store::Order { id: 1, item: "coffee".to_string(), qty: 2 };
    store::save(&order).expect("save order");
}

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F007">
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F008" PATH="src/store.rs" LINES="25">
use std::io;

/// One order as the kiosk records it.
pub struct Order {
    pub id: u32,
    pub item: String,
    pub qty: u32,
}

/// Write the order to orders/<id>.tsv.
pub fn save(order: &Order) -> io::Result<()> {
    std::fs::create_dir_all("orders")?;
    std::fs::write(format!("orders/{}.tsv", order.id), encode(order))
}

/// One tab-separated line with a checksum of the item name.
fn encode(order: &Order) -> String {
    format!("{}\t{}\t{}\t{:08x}\n", order.id, order.item, order.qty, checksum(&order.item))
}

/// FNV-1a over the bytes of the text.
fn checksum(text: &str) -> u32 {
    text.bytes().fold(0x811c9dc5, |hash, byte| (hash ^ u32::from(byte)).wrapping_mul(0x0100_0193))
}

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F008">
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F009" PATH="src/util.rs" LINES="14">
/// The greeting shown on the kiosk screen.
pub fn greet(name: &str) -> String {
    format!("Hello, {}!", title_case(name))
}

/// Upper-case the first letter of a name, leave the rest as typed.
pub fn title_case(name: &str) -> String {
    let mut chars = name.chars();
    match chars.next() {
        Some(first) => first.to_uppercase().chain(chars).collect(),
        None => String::new(),
    }
}

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F009">
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F011" PATH="tools/report.py" LINES="19">
"""Sum the quantities of every saved order: python3 tools/report.py orders/"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def read_orders(folder):
    for path in sorted(Path(folder).glob("*.tsv")):
        order_id, item, qty, _checksum = path.read_text().rstrip("\n").split("\t")
        yield order_id, item, int(qty)


def main(folder="orders"):
    total = sum(qty for _, _, qty in read_orders(folder))
    print(f"{total} items")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(*sys.argv[1:])

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F011">
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F013" PATH="web/app.ts" LINES="20">
import { formatName, formatPrice } from "./format";

interface Line {
  item: string;
  cents: number;
  qty: number;
}

/** The greeting banner of the kiosk web screen. */
export function renderGreeting(name: string): string {
  return `Hello, ${formatName(name)}!`;
}

/** One receipt line per order line, then the total. */
export function renderReceipt(lines: Line[]): string[] {
  const rows = lines.map((l) => `${l.qty} x ${l.item}  ${formatPrice(l.cents * l.qty)}`);
  const total = lines.reduce((sum, l) => sum + l.cents * l.qty, 0);
  return [...rows, `total  ${formatPrice(total)}`];
}

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F013">
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F014" PATH="web/format.ts" LINES="10">
/** Price in cents to a display string, e.g. 250 -> "2.50 EUR". */
export function formatPrice(cents: number, currency = "EUR"): string {
  return `${(cents / 100).toFixed(2)} ${currency}`;
}

/** The customer's name as the screen shows it. */
export function formatName(name: string): string {
  return name.trim() === "" ? "guest" : name.trim();
}

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F014">pack bytes=5548 files=11 retention=stdout version=V1
```

```text
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F004" PATH="README.md" LINES="19">
# kiosk

A tiny order kiosk. It is the example project that every command on the dctx website runs on.

## Run

    cargo run -- ada

prints `Hello, Ada!` and saves order 1 to `orders/1.tsv`.

## Orders

Each order is one tab-separated line: id, item, quantity and a checksum of the item name.
`python3 tools/report.py orders/` sums the quantities.

## Configuration

`config.toml` holds the currency and the screen title. Secrets live in `.env`, which is never committed.

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F004">

title = "kiosk example"
currency = "EUR"
```

---
url: https://www.dctx.internet.technology/templates/
title: default.dctx_template
source: https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/crates/dctx-template/templates/default.dctx_template

```text
# ==============================================================================
# DCTX TEMPLATE DEFINITION V1
# ==============================================================================
# This file defines how the LLM context is formatted.
# It consists of three sections: [VARIABLES], [PARTIALS], and [LAYOUT].
#
# SYNTAX GUIDE:
# - {{VAR_NAME}}      : Inserts a configuration variable defined in [VARIABLES].
# - {{{DATA_FIELD}}}  : Inserts dynamic data from the project (e.g., file content).
#
# ==============================================================================

[VARIABLES]
# --- 1. Syntactic Markers (Granular Control) ---
# Defines the exact characters used to wrap tags.
# Allows handling XML, HTML, or Custom formats safely.
start_marker_open  = "<"
start_marker_close = ">"
end_marker_open    = "</"
end_marker_close   = ">"

# --- 2. Semantic Marker Names ---
# Defines the keywords used inside the tags.
instr_marker         = "INSTRUCTIONS"
tree_start_marker    = "DIRECTORY_TREE"
tree_end_marker      = "DIRECTORY_TREE"
file_start_marker    = "FILE_CONTENT_START"
file_end_marker      = "FILE_CONTENT_END"

# --- 3. Attribute Keys ---
# Used inside tags to denote properties.
attr_id    = "ID"
attr_path  = "PATH"
attr_size  = "SIZE"
attr_lines = "LINES"
attr_mod   = "MOD"

# --- 4. Branding & Header Config ---
folder_denotation_marker = "DIRECTORY"

# --- 5. Instructions Block Text ---
# This text explains the format to the LLM. It references the variables above
# to ensure the instructions always match the actual format used.
# Use '\n' for new lines.
instructions_text = "1. Manifest: The {{start_marker_open}}{{tree_start_marker}}{{start_marker_close}} section lists all files.\n   - Each entry: [TYPE] RELATIVE_PATH ({{attr_id}}:UNIQUE_ID)\n   - TYPE is [D] for directory, [F] for file.\n2. Content Access: To read a specific file:\n   - Find its UNIQUE_ID from the directory tree.\n   - Search for the marker: {{start_marker_open}}{{file_start_marker}} {{attr_id}}=\"UNIQUE_ID\"{{start_marker_close}}\n   - The content is between this marker and {{end_marker_open}}{{file_end_marker}} {{attr_id}}=\"UNIQUE_ID\"{{end_marker_close}}"

# ==============================================================================
# [PARTIALS]
# Defines the look of repeated elements (Tree items and Files).
# ==============================================================================

# --- Tree Entry Partial ---
# Context: 'node' object
# Available Data: {{{node.type_char}}}, {{{node.path}}}, {{{node.id}}}, {{{node.mod}}}, {{{node.size}}}
# The default entry leaves {{{node.mod}}} and {{{node.size_part}}} out: a timestamp or a size changes on an edit or a touch
# and would break the byte-stable prefix of the page. Custom templates may still use {{attr_mod}}, {{{node.mod}}},
# {{{node.size}}} and {{{node.size_part}}}; `--tree-stamps=on` selects the stamped built-in (the 1.0.0 text).
[PARTIAL:TREE_ENTRY]
{{{node.type_char}}} {{{node.path}}} ({{attr_id}}:{{{node.id}}})

# --- File Block Partial ---
# Context: 'file' object
# Available Data: {{{file.id}}}, {{{file.path}}}, {{{file.lines}}}, {{{file.size}}}, {{{file.content}}}
[PARTIAL:FILE_BLOCK]
{{start_marker_open}}{{file_start_marker}} {{attr_id}}="{{{file.id}}}" {{attr_path}}="{{{file.path}}}" {{attr_lines}}="{{{file.lines}}}"{{start_marker_close}}
{{{file.content}}}
{{end_marker_open}}{{file_end_marker}} {{attr_id}}="{{{file.id}}}"{{end_marker_close}}

# ==============================================================================
# [LAYOUT]
# The master structure of the final output file.
# Note: The Version Header (e.g. [DCTX_SNAPSHOT_V1]) is hardcoded in the binary
# and NOT included here.
# ==============================================================================
[LAYOUT]
[{{folder_denotation_marker}}:{{{project}}}]

{{start_marker_open}}{{instr_marker}}{{start_marker_close}}
{{instructions_text}}
{{end_marker_open}}{{instr_marker}}{{end_marker_close}}

{{start_marker_open}}{{tree_start_marker}}{{start_marker_close}}
{{{comp.tree}}}
{{end_marker_open}}{{tree_end_marker}}{{end_marker_close}}

{{{comp.files}}}
```

---
url: https://www.dctx.internet.technology/templates/
title: stamped.dctx_template
source: https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/crates/dctx-template/templates/stamped.dctx_template
---

```text
# ==============================================================================
# DCTX TEMPLATE DEFINITION V1
# ==============================================================================
# This file defines how the LLM context is formatted.
# It consists of three sections: [VARIABLES], [PARTIALS], and [LAYOUT].
#
# SYNTAX GUIDE:
# - {{VAR_NAME}}      : Inserts a configuration variable defined in [VARIABLES].
# - {{{DATA_FIELD}}}  : Inserts dynamic data from the project (e.g., file content).
#
# ==============================================================================

[VARIABLES]
# --- 1. Syntactic Markers (Granular Control) ---
# Defines the exact characters used to wrap tags.
# Allows handling XML, HTML, or Custom formats safely.
start_marker_open  = "<"
start_marker_close = ">"
end_marker_open    = "</"
end_marker_close   = ">"

# --- 2. Semantic Marker Names ---
# Defines the keywords used inside the tags.
instr_marker         = "INSTRUCTIONS"
tree_start_marker    = "DIRECTORY_TREE"
tree_end_marker      = "DIRECTORY_TREE"
file_start_marker    = "FILE_CONTENT_START"
file_end_marker      = "FILE_CONTENT_END"

# --- 3. Attribute Keys ---
# Used inside tags to denote properties.
attr_id    = "ID"
attr_path  = "PATH"
attr_size  = "SIZE"
attr_lines = "LINES"
attr_mod   = "MOD"

# --- 4. Branding & Header Config ---
folder_denotation_marker = "DIRECTORY"

# --- 5. Instructions Block Text ---
# This text explains the format to the LLM. It references the variables above
# to ensure the instructions always match the actual format used.
# Use '\n' for new lines.
instructions_text = "1. Manifest: The {{start_marker_open}}{{tree_start_marker}}{{start_marker_close}} section lists all files.\n   - Each entry: [TYPE] RELATIVE_PATH ({{attr_id}}:UNIQUE_ID, {{attr_mod}}:TIMESTAMP)\n   - TYPE is [D] for directory, [F] for file.\n2. Content Access: To read a specific file:\n   - Find its UNIQUE_ID from the directory tree.\n   - Search for the marker: {{start_marker_open}}{{file_start_marker}} {{attr_id}}=\"UNIQUE_ID\"{{start_marker_close}}\n   - The content is between this marker and {{end_marker_open}}{{file_end_marker}} {{attr_id}}=\"UNIQUE_ID\"{{end_marker_close}}"

# ==============================================================================
# [PARTIALS]
# Defines the look of repeated elements (Tree items and Files).
# ==============================================================================

# --- Tree Entry Partial ---
# Context: 'node' object
# Available Data: {{{node.type_char}}}, {{{node.path}}}, {{{node.id}}}, {{{node.mod}}}, {{{node.size}}}
[PARTIAL:TREE_ENTRY]
{{{node.type_char}}} {{{node.path}}} ({{attr_id}}:{{{node.id}}}, {{attr_mod}}:{{{node.mod}}}{{{node.size_part}}})

# --- File Block Partial ---
# Context: 'file' object
# Available Data: {{{file.id}}}, {{{file.path}}}, {{{file.lines}}}, {{{file.size}}}, {{{file.content}}}
[PARTIAL:FILE_BLOCK]
{{start_marker_open}}{{file_start_marker}} {{attr_id}}="{{{file.id}}}" {{attr_path}}="{{{file.path}}}" {{attr_lines}}="{{{file.lines}}}"{{start_marker_close}}
{{{file.content}}}
{{end_marker_open}}{{file_end_marker}} {{attr_id}}="{{{file.id}}}"{{end_marker_close}}

# ==============================================================================
# [LAYOUT]
# The master structure of the final output file.
# Note: The Version Header (e.g. [DCTX_SNAPSHOT_V1]) is hardcoded in the binary
# and NOT included here.
# ==============================================================================
[LAYOUT]
[{{folder_denotation_marker}}:{{{project}}}]

{{start_marker_open}}{{instr_marker}}{{start_marker_close}}
{{instructions_text}}
{{end_marker_open}}{{instr_marker}}{{end_marker_close}}

{{start_marker_open}}{{tree_start_marker}}{{start_marker_close}}
{{{comp.tree}}}
{{end_marker_open}}{{tree_end_marker}}{{end_marker_close}}

{{{comp.files}}}
```

# Changelog

All notable changes to dctx are recorded here. The format follows
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/); versions follow
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/). Dates are ISO 8601.

The open repository is ongoing work. Anything that still depends on third-party
crates is not considered enterprise-ready; enterprise-ready builds are part of
dctx Enterprise.

## [Unreleased]

## [1.1.0] - 2026-11-06

Release **1.1.0** (`v1.1.0`; release candidate `v1.1.0-rc1` 2026-11-04). It folds in the 1.0.1 line, which was never released on its own.

### Since rc1 (docs, CI, tooling and SPDX licence headers only; no change to dctx output)

- **Docs**: byte stability re-measured on 2026-11-06 — 33/33 text and 33/33 JSON map answers identical
  after unrelated edits and over five runs (see docs/research/stability-20261105/REPORT.md);
  SPEC and README status texts updated, historical 0/63 kept.
- **Formal**: the plugin TLC gate accepts the newer TLC wording 'Temporal property X was violated.' /
  'Invariant X was violated.' (all 8 baselines, 59 mutants, 37 witnesses pass); host-specific
  tla2tools.jar paths removed; TLC trace files ignored.
- **Self-hosted CI** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): the job run step by step on a self-hosted Linux runner (16 cores) from a clean
  `git archive` of the commit; results and badge recorded in `docs/ci/RESULTS.md` — 2279 run, 2279 passed, 0 skipped.
- **Third-party npm licence inventory**: `scripts/npm_licenses.py` indexes every repository `package-lock.json` into
  `THIRD_PARTY_NPM.md`; `npm_licenses.py --check` runs in CI and fails on a disallowed licence or a stale report.

### Added

- **Perl** (`.pl`, `.pm`, `.t`, `.psgi`): `package A::B;` and `package A { .. }` as `type` symbols holding every later
  `sub` (named `A::B::name`) as `fn` symbols (`guess` confidence, full tier). POD is masked like a comment; call edges
  come from `name(..)`, bareword calls with an argument and `&name`, never after `->`, `sub` or a sigil.
- **Fortran** (`.f90`, `.f95`, `.f03`, `.f08`, `.f`, `.for`): `module`, derived `type` and named `interface` as `type`
  symbols; `program`, `function` and `subroutine` as `fn` symbols named `module::name` (`guess` confidence, full tier).
  Keywords are case-insensitive, `!` comments only, fixed-form column rules are not modelled; call edges skip
  intrinsic and control keywords that precede `(`.
- **Verilog/SystemVerilog** (`.v`, `.vh`, `.sv`, `.svh`): `module`, `macromodule`, `interface`, `package` and `class`
  declarations as `type` outline symbols and `function`/`task` declarations as `fn` symbols (`guess` confidence, full tier),
  with module-scope call edges and `<module> <instance> (` instantiation links resolved through the call index.
- **Prefix-stable `pack` output** (DCX-P-PACK): tree lines carry the `ID` only, with no `MOD:` and no `SIZE:`, so a
  bare `touch` leaves the page byte-identical and an edit keeps everything before the edited file as a shared prefix
  for prompt caches. `--tree-stamps=on|off` (default `off`) selects the built-in tree template; `on` reproduces the
  1.0.0 bytes. The desktop tree-only export keeps its digest line last, behind a stable lead line.
- **Stat stamps in the manifest** (DCX-P-STAMP): a stamp pass runs before the digest, with a racy-timestamp guard; a
  touch-only change is decided by content. A gate replays 200 random edits against a cold rebuild.
- **Record and entry caps** (DCX-P-CACHE): checked during the scan and set by `DCTX_MAX_RECORDS` and
  `DCTX_MAX_ENTRIES`; the cache is reclaimed on publish, evicts before refusing, and readers share one lock.
- **Open-source maintenance model** (DCX-OSS): `MAINTENANCE.md`, `TRADEMARK.md`, a DCO in
  `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `FUNDING.yml`; the desktop app is open source too.

### Changed

- **Id lookup** (DCX-P-IDX) uses a sorted hash index instead of a linear node scan.
- Large source files were split into submodules by pure moves (400-line rule): `pack.rs`, `path.rs`, `reuse.rs`,
  `bound.rs`, `plugin.rs`, `yaml.rs` and others. No behaviour change.
- The version is **1.1.0** for every `crates/*` and `plugins/*` package; the desktop app stays on 0.11.0.

### Fixed

- A closed stdout pipe (`dctx pack | head`) exits 0 without a panic.

## [1.0.0] — 2026-10-31

The first v1 release, folded from the 0.26 development line. Every `crates/*` and
`plugins/*` package, `VERSION`, `project-meta.yaml` and the README badge are at **1.0.0**
(`tools/sync-version.sh --check` keeps them and their `Cargo.lock` entries together). The
desktop app keeps its own version line (0.11.0) and its own release workflow.

### Shipped surface
- **Map verbs**: `dctx map map | find | neighbors | explain | read | skeleton | grep | hubs | path | export`,
  with hard token budgets, stable ids, cursor paging and precision labels; call and import edges are lexical.
- **`dctx mcp`**: a stdio MCP server exposing the map verbs as tools.
- **`dctx pack`**: the whole project as one structured block to stdout, the clipboard or `--output`.
- **`dctx pack --for "<text>" --budget N`**: task context for an agent card: `map find` on the names the text mentions,
  then neighbors and read of the best hits, whole lines only, within N estimated tokens (ceil(2 × UTF-8 bytes / 7),
  default 3000). `tools/cardgen/context.sh` prepends it to a card; `docs/guides/AGENTS-SNIPPET.md` is the `AGENTS.md` section that tells agents to run it first;
  `tools/cardgen/dogfood.py` records before/after prompt tokens for the ten v1 cards.
- **`dctx languages`**: one registry with three tiers (full, outline, docs) that also renders the README table.
- **Privacy deny**: sensitive files (env files, keys, credentials, ...), `.git` at any depth and symlinks are
  never read or printed by `pack`, any map verb or `mcp`; there is no override flag. Detection is by file name only.
- **Determinism**: two fresh indexes give byte-identical answers, and an unrelated edit changes only `hubs`;
  `scripts/release-check.sh` gates both, and counts network syscalls under `strace -f` (must be zero).
- **`dctx --version`** prints `dctx 1.0.0 (<git sha>)`; the sha is embedded at build time, `unknown` without git.
- **README benchmark section** rendered from the committed run 7 JSON by `scripts/render_readme.py`;
  `just readme-check` fails when the README differs.

### Out of scope for v1
- Any network or cloud feature.
- macOS and Windows support claims (untested); Linux x86_64 is the only tested platform.
- Watch or incremental mode beyond re-indexing.
- Fortran and Verilog (both shipped in 1.1.0).
- Shell call edges.
- Embeddings and semantic search.
- LSP-grade type resolution.
- A stable plugin ABI and desktop API (unstable, not a v1 contract).
- Cross-repository queries.
- Publishing to crates.io or GitHub (an owner decision).

### Added
- **Call and import edges** in the map index: `dctx map neighbors --edge calls|imports`
  now answers who calls what, resolved by lexical scope, imports and module paths, with
  `name`/`guess` confidence; ambiguous references are dropped.
- **New map verbs**: `skeleton <file>` (declaration signatures, no bodies), `grep <literal>`
  (hits grouped by enclosing symbol), `hubs` (most-called symbols and per-directory counts),
  `path <FROM> <TO>` (shortest edge path) and `export --format json|mermaid` (the whole graph).
  `neighbors --depth` goes up to 4 (breadth-first, each node once).
- **`dctx mcp`**: a stdio MCP server exposing the map verbs as tools.
- **`dctx languages`** (`--json`, `--markdown`): every supported language with its tag, file names, tier
  (full: symbols and lexical call edges; outline: symbols only; docs: sections) and confidence, from one facade
  registry (`dctx::LANGUAGES`) that also feeds `--version --verbose` and the README table, which a test diffs.
- **A CLI exit-code contract** (`docs/CLI-EXIT-CODES.md`) for `map`, `pack`, `mcp`, `languages` and unknown
  commands: 0 ok, 1 no result (an id not in the index, a binary file target, nothing to pack), 2 usage, 3 index
  error. Every failure prints a `hint:` line. Previously every failure exited 1. A non-UTF-8 argument is now a
  usage error instead of a panic, an unknown flag is named as unknown, and `dctx map <verb> --help` prints a page
  with an `Example:` line for each map verb.
- **Outline symbols (`guess` confidence) for 25 more formats**: Scala, Dart, Zig, Solidity,
  Gleam, Groovy; Elixir, Lua, OCaml, R, Julia, Haskell; Terraform/HCL, SQL, shell, Makefile,
  Dockerfile, protobuf, Pascal, GraphQL; and headed sections for `.txt`, `.rst`, `.adoc`,
  `.org` and `.tex` documents.
- **A three-way benchmark against graphify and Trail-Code** (`docs/BENCHMARK-20261030.md`)
  and the gap matrix behind it (`docs/GAP-MATRIX-20261030.md`).

- **dctx Desktop is free, forever** for individuals, teams and companies
  ([announcement](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/news/desktop-free-forever/)).
- **The dctx Context Management Specification** (`docs/SPEC.md`): prompt-processing
  efficiency as the core belief, the ten RAG defect classes and how dctx rules
  them out, the seven-layer organization policy, prefix-stable tiers and delta
  answers, the persistent index, the plugin boundary and the roadmap.
- **An isolated, reproducible benchmark against Trail-Code**
  (`docs/research/trail-code-2026-10/`): methodology, raw data, scripts and
  numbered findings.
- **Map mode** (`dctx map`): `map`, `find`, `neighbors`, `explain` and `read`
  with hard token budgets (up to 2,000 per answer), cursor paging, stable ids,
  explicit `moved`/`gone`/`ambiguous` outcomes and precision labels on every answer.
- First-party structural extractors for JavaScript, TypeScript/TSX, Python, Go,
  Java, C/C++, C#, Kotlin, Ruby, PHP, Swift, Markdown and JSON/TOML/YAML; Rust
  through `syn`.
- A verified map generation reused across CLI invocations.
- **Plugin host**: capability grants, consent, receipts, liveness by progress,
  signed distribution verified with Ed25519, and Linux confinement; the bundled
  **Git plugin** (`.gitignore` protection and consented staging).
- **Cache lifecycle**: time-based expiry, a system size cap and a bounded
  automatic cleaner (`dctx cache status | gc | purge | config | auto`).
- `dctx pack`: an explicit pack to stdout, the clipboard or `--output`, without
  leaving files in the project.
- The template system's v2 compiler (a sealed plan IR) and organization ceilings.
- `crates/dctx`: one library facade for the CLI, the desktop app and future
  bindings.
- A new website with changelog and news, and the dctx film
  (`presentation/video/`).

### Changed
- **Byte-stable map answers**: the text header is `# <place> <verb>` and JSON no longer
  carries `snapshot`, `generation` or `freshness.age_s`, so answers stay identical across
  unrelated edits (prompt-cache friendly). `--meta` restores the old fields.
- **`dctx pack` never prints env-shaped files** (`.env`, `.env.*`, `*.env`, `.envrc`); they
  stay in the tree by name with their content omitted.
- **Strict sensitive-file deny for every command**: besides env files, `*.pem`, `*.key`,
  `*.p12`, `*.pfx`, `*.jks`, `*.keystore`, SSH private keys (`id_rsa`, `id_ed25519`, ...),
  `credentials`, `credentials.json`, `secrets.yaml` (and other data extensions), `.npmrc`,
  `.netrc`, `.pypirc`, `.pgpass`, `.htpasswd` and `.git-credentials` are never read or printed
  by `pack`, any `dctx map` verb (by id or raw path, with or without `--in`) or `dctx mcp`.
  There is no override flag (see ADR-014).
- **`.git` is closed for good**: a `.git` segment at any depth is never listed or read by the map
  verbs and never read by `pack`, even when `.gitignore` or `.dctxignore` says `!.git/`.
- **No symlink escapes**: `FsSource` opens files with `O_NOFOLLOW`, requires a regular file
  handle, and refuses symlinked directories, so a symlink swapped in after the stat cannot leak
  bytes from outside the root.
- `DCTX_INDEX_IGNORED=1` (ignore files are not applied) is now documented in ADR-014; the
  sensitive-file deny, the `.git` guard and the symlink rules still apply when it is set.
- **Total-source ceiling raised from 64 MiB to 1 GiB**; `DCTX_MAX_SOURCE_BYTES` overrides it.
- The core never reads `.git/`, never spawns `git` and never uses VCS object ids;
  content identity is dctx's own SHA-256 (`crates/dctx-hash`).
- Repository ignore rules are applied before any read on the map path, and
  `--lines A-B` returns exact line ranges.
- Everything in the repository is licensed under Apache-2.0.

### Fixed
- Node spans resolve from one newline index per file instead of rescanning the
  source for every symbol (cold `find` on a 3,000-file repository: 141 s → about 6 s).
- Queries share one generation instead of cloning it (peak memory down by about
  30 % on the same repository).
- One hostile file no longer fails every map verb for the whole repository: a Rust
  file that is not UTF-8 is indexed as a module with no symbols (like every other
  language), and a file name the confined path cannot carry (a backslash) is skipped
  and marks the snapshot `partial`, as `pack` already did.

### Known issues
Measured in the benchmarks and scheduled in the specification's roadmap:
- No incremental indexing: the first query after an edit re-indexes, and each
  edit adds a full generation to the cache.
- Outline-tier formats carry symbols and `contains` edges only; heuristic families are
  labelled `guess`. `dctx languages` lists the tier and confidence of every format.
- The 70-question task protocol (run 7: 140/140) was designed by the dctx team; an
  independently selected protocol (v1 card 6) is pending.

## [0.25.0] — 2026-05-29

The last release of the first Rust generation, with **zero third-party
dependencies** in the core and the CLI.

### Added
- Snapshot, diff and tree modes; clipboard output; an interactive TUI.
- Filters by extension, size, content and visibility; binary detection.
- Ahead-of-time compiled output templates.
- The privacy guarantee: ignored files are never read, not even in debug mode;
  omit rules list a file without reading its content.
- The desktop app (Tauri) on the shared core.

## [0.11.0] — 2026-01-26

### Added
- A redesigned desktop interface with light and dark modes.
- A sequential, fail-fast CI pipeline.

## [0.10.0] — 2026-01-25

### Added
- Advanced CLI filters and their documentation.

## [0.1.0] — 2026-01-08

### Added
- The Rust rewrite of `dircontxt` begins.

## dircontxt [1.0.0] — 2025-11-15

The original tool, written in pure C (`legacy-c/`).

### Added
- One LLM-ready `.llmcontext.txt` snapshot with a manifest and unique ids for
  every file and directory, plus a binary state file.
- Automatic versioning with diffs that carry only the changed files.
- A three-tier ignore system (built-in defaults, a global ignore file and a
  per-project `.dircontxtignore`) and a global configuration file.
